title: Targeted Activation of ROBO1 Mitigates Age-Related Osteoporosis by Enhancing Autophagic Flux.
abstract: Age-related osteoporosis is driven by an imbalance in bone remodeling, yet the underlying cellular mechanisms governing osteoblast dysfunction remain incompletely understood. This study identifies ROBO1 as a crucial regulator of osteogenesis whose expression is significantly downregulated in aged bone tissue and senescent osteoblasts. In vitro, Robo1 knockdown impairs bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2)-induced osteogenic differentiation and attenuates canonical SMAD1 phosphorylation. Mechanistically, molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation assays reveal that internalized BMP2 physically interacts with ROBO1 to trigger autophagic activation. Strikingly, pharmacological restoration of autophagy with rapamycin rescues the osteogenic defects in Robo1-deficient cells. Conversely, ROBO1 overexpression robustly enhances osteogenic differentiation by driving downstream autophagic flux without detectable changes in mTOR phosphorylation, an effect that is abolished by targeted autophagic blockade. In vivo, the activation of endogenous ROBO1 via adeno-associated virus (AAV)-small activating RNA (saRNA) injections in aged mouse bone marrow significantly rejuvenates osteoblast activity, suppresses osteoclastogenesis, and significantly improves trabecular bone mass and microarchitecture. In conclusion, the age-related decline of ROBO1 contributes to skeletal deterioration by impairing the BMP2-driven autophagic axis. These findings elucidate novel mechanisms of bone homeostasis and h
summary_short: Mechanistically, molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation assays reveal that internalized BMP2 physically interacts with ROBO1 to trigger autophagic activation.

title: Chrono-Therapeutics in Type 2 Diabetes: Translational Perspectives Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Integrated Optimization of Pharmacological, Nutritional, and Lifestyle Interventions.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a multisystem endocrine disorder that requires multidisciplinary management in solving its global health challenge, as its prevalence increases despite the scientific advances in therapeutic and dietary interventions. The management strategies are expected to be personalized rather than "one-size-fits-all", as their efficacy has declined over time. This occurred because of the often-overlooked significance of circadian rhythms, despite their physiological roles in energy balance, endocrine, and β-cell function. The misalignment of pharmaceutical interventions, nutrition, and lifestyle with the biological clock contributes to and complicates T2DM. The advent of Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has now enabled comprehensive assessment of glycemic variability over a long period, allowing monitoring of the impact of nutrition, physical activity, and therapy. CGM has been shown to improve the precision of therapeutic interventions in alignment with the physiological clock. This will potentially enhance efficacy, minimize adverse effects, and improve long-term metabolic outcomes. However, several articles have separately explored chronotherapeutic, chrononutrition, and lifestyle modification for T2DM management, without a clinically integrated framework. This review, from a translational perspective, integrates circadian rhythms, chronotherapeutic interventions, chronotyping, lifestyle factors, and gene variants associated with glycemic dysregu

title: Probiotic Supplementation Reduces Waist Circumference in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently associated with excess adiposity and increased cardiometabolic risk. Although probiotic supplementation has been investigated as a strategy for the metabolic management of T2DM, its effects on anthropometric outcomes remain inconsistent, and waist circumference (WC), a clinically relevant measure of central adiposity, has been less frequently evaluated than other anthropometric outcomes in evidence syntheses. Objective To investigate the effects of probiotic supplementation on anthropometric outcomes in patients with T2DM, with particular emphasis on WC as a clinically relevant indicator of central adiposity. Materials and methods This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023480243), and was conducted in accordance with a previously published protocol. Randomized clinical trials were identified through searches of the PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using fixed- or random-effects models, depending on the degree of statistical heterogeneity (I 2 ), and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test, where applicable. Results Twenty-two randomized controlled trials were included. Probiotic supplementation had no significant overall effect on body weight or BMI. summary_short: Introduction Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently associated with excess adiposity and increased cardiometabolic risk.

title: Sarcopenia, Sarcopenic Obesity and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Challenges in Management-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has become the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Sarcopenia, obesity and the co-existent condition of sarcopenic obesity are highly prevalent in patients with MASLD due to shared pathophysiology of these conditions. Weight loss is a shared aim for management of obesity and MASLD but can potentiate sarcopenia, which continues to be under-recognised in these populations. There are many promising emerging pharmacotherapies under investigation for treatment of MASLD; however, most studies do not explore changes in body composition. This narrative review summarises the key pathophysiological principles and management pillars for these conditions and highlights the challenges faced by clinicians and patients in managing MASLD and risk of potentiating sarcopenic obesity.
summary_short: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has become the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Sarcopenia, obesity and the co-existent condition of sarcopenic obesity are highly prevalent in patients with MASLD due to shared pathophysiology of these conditions.

title: Position of De Novo Purine Biosynthesis Gene Disruptions Shapes Purine-Starvation Phenotype in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
abstract: Purine starvation induces a quiescence-like, stress-resistant physiological state in Saccharomyces cerevisiae but it remains unclear whether this response is uniform across disruptions of the de novo purine biosynthesis pathway. Here, we used a pathway-position series of adenine-biosynthesis deletion mutants to test how the location of the metabolic blockage shapes cellular adaptation to purine starvation using nitrogen starvation as a reference condition. Across mutants, purine starvation induced a shared core response, marked by reduced growth, repression of ribosome biogenesis and rRNA-processing modules, and accumulation of cells in the G1/G0 phase. However, the response's magnitude and composition varied systematically with pathway position. Early pathway mutants showed the strongest desiccation tolerance and stress-associated transcriptional remodeling, whereas late-pathway mutants showed weaker protection. The ade16Δade17Δ double mutant was a distinct outlier with altered carbon-flux distribution and limited stress resilience, suggesting that late-pathway disruption produces a physiologically different starvation state. Transcriptome analysis showed partial overlap with nitrogen starvation, but also with pathway-position-dependent regulation of metabolic, ribosome-related, mitochondrial, and stress-response modules. Clinical and Biochemical Predictors of Menstrual Response to Metformin in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: Development of a Simplified Prediction Score.
abstract: Aims Metformin improves menstrual regularity in women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; previously polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS), but its effect varies widely between individuals. This study aimed to identify the clinical and biochemical factors influencing this response and to use them to build a practical predictive model. Methods In this prospective, single-arm, single-center cohort study, 541 women with PMOS diagnosed by Rotterdam criteria received metformin 500 mg twice daily for up to 6 months alongside standardized lifestyle counseling. Responders were defined as regular cycles (21-35 days) for two consecutive cycles between months 3 and 6. Clinical and biochemical variables were compared between responders and non-responders, and independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, then combined into an additive point-based model for individualized response prediction. Results Of 541 participants, 240 (44.4%) were responders. Such a tool could help clinicians set realistic expectations and consider alternative therapy earlier for patients unlikely to benefit. External validation in independent cohorts is the logica

title: Genomic Differentiation Between Kazakh Whiteheaded and Hereford Cattle.
abstract: Kazakh Whiteheaded (Bos taurus; KWH) cattle represent a composite breed developed under harsh continental conditions, yet their genomic differentiation from Hereford (Bos taurus; HFD) remains poorly understood. The aim of this study was to investigate population structure, gene flow, and genomic differentiation between KWH and HFD using genome-wide SNP data. A dataset of 48 KWH individuals genotyped with the Illumina BovineSNP50 BeadChip was analysed together with a global reference panel. Population structure and gene flow were assessed using TreeMix and f-statistics, and genetic differentiation was evaluated using SNP-based FST analysis. Runs of homozygosity (ROH) and XP-nSL analyses were additionally used to characterize genomic regions potentially affected by selection. Genome-wide differentiation between KWH and HFD was low (mean FST ≈0.02-0.03), indicating a close genetic relationship. Phylogenetic analyses consistently placed KWH within the taurine lineage, and no migration edges involving KWH were detected. However, f-statistics revealed a weak but significant indicine-related signal. A subset of loci exhibited elevated FST values, forming distinct peaks across the genome. Overlap between highly differentiated loci and ROH islands was limited, while integration of FST, ROH and XP-nSL identified a single concordant signal. These results indicate that KWH has a predominantly taurine genetic background with limited evidence of recent gene flow. Genomic divergence from HF
summary_short: These results indicate that KWH has a predominantly taurine genetic background with limited evidence of recent gene flow.

title: Adaptive glycolysis buffers skeletal muscle insulin action against mitochondrial dysfunction
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is widely considered a driver of skeletal muscle insulin resistance. Using a muscle-specific MIPEP knockout model, Cutler et al. demonstrate that compensatory glycolysis sustains glucose uptake despite impaired insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation, revealing metabolic flexibility as a key determinant of insulin sensitivity in the context of mitochondrial dysfunction.

title: Restoring the perception–action cycle in frail older adults through cognitive–motor dual-task training
abstract: Cognitive–Motor Dual-Task Training (CMDT) may promote cognitive and functional benefits in older adults; however, its effects on the neural mechanisms supporting adaptive perception–action control remain unclear. Previous analyses from the same randomized controlled trial showed that CMDT restores anticipatory control mechanisms in frail older adults. Here, we investigated whether these adaptations extend to post-stimulus stages of information processing. Thirty frail and pre-frail older adults were randomly assigned to either a CMDT group or a motor-training control group and completed an 8-week intervention. High-density electroencephalography was recorded at baseline, mid-intervention, and post-intervention while participants performed a visuomotor Go/No-go task. Analyses focused on the P1, N1, prefrontal P2 (pP2), and P3 event-related potential components. No training-related effects were observed on P1 or P3 amplitudes. In contrast, significant Group × Time interactions emerged for N1 and pP2. The CMDT group showed progressive increases in N1 amplitude, suggesting enhanced attentional selection, and increased pP2 amplitude, indicating improved stimulus–response integration and perception–action coupling. No comparable changes were observed in the control group. An exploratory Perception–Action Cycle Index further revealed a robust, progressive, and individually consistent pattern of coordinated adaptation across proactive and reactive ERP markers in the CMDT group. title: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Pharmacotherapy after Acute Coronary Syndrome: Evidence Boundaries and an Expert Framework.
abstract: To review cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) pharmacotherapy after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), distinguishing established treatment indications from evidence for initiation immediately after myocardial infarction (MI). This targeted narrative review used PubMed/MEDLINE searches through August 17, 2026, with verification of pivotal trials, guidelines, and prescribing information. An atherosclerotic MI establishes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and fulfils the ASCVD component of a treatment indication. Additional eligibility depends on the patient's characteristics and the selected therapy. Dedicated early post-MI trials have mainly studied sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. EMMY assessed a biomarker outcome. The hierarchical primary composite in DAPA-MI favoured dapagliflozin (win ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.20-1.50), mainly through cardiometabolic outcomes; the composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization was not significantly reduced. EMPACT-MI did not demonstrate a significant reduction in its primary composite of first HF hospitalization or all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.76-1.06). SGLT2 inhibitor, semaglutide, and finerenone trials support treatment in defined stable ASCVD, obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or HF populations. title: Psychosocial, dietary and behavioural experiences of adults using GLP-1 receptor agonists for weight management: A qualitative study.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have transformed obesity management by delivering substantial biomedical benefits, yet the lived experience of GLP-1 RA users remains poorly understood. Existing research has centered on people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and emphasised biomedical outcomes with limited exploration of how people using it for weight management experience the psychosocial, dietary, and behavioural changes accompanying pharmacological weight loss. Understanding the user experience is vital to inform person-centered care, which may critically shape long-term treatment success. Therefore, this qualitative study aimed to explore the experiences of adults using GLP-1 RAs for weight management, and how these changes influence wellbeing, identity, support needs, and adherence. Adults with obesity, but not T2DM, were recruited in Australia via purposive self-selection as part of a larger trial (GLP-1 and Dietary adjustments feasibility study). Thirteen participants (aged 25-65; 10 female, three male) completed semi-structured interviews online after three months of GLP-1 RA use. Transcripts were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Six themes were identified: legitimising treatment; reconfiguring eating practices; building health beyond weight; balancing cost and care; weathering stigma and blame; and navigating information and support. title: Exploring the Link Between Artificial Sweetener Consumption and COPD: Insights From NHANES Data, Machine Learning, Multi-Omics, and Experimental Validation.
abstract: Artificial sweeteners (AS) are an emerging environmental pollutant. Few studies have focused on the link between AS consumption and the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). This study integrates NHANES, GEO, and sceQTL data, utilizing methods such as longitudinal studies, toxicity analysis, machine learning, MR analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments to investigate the relationship between AS consumption and COPD risk, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms. NHANES data analysis showed an association between AS consumption and increased COPD risk. Toxicity predictions indicated that AS exhibits respiratory toxicity, with several AS compounds posing acute toxicity risks to susceptible populations under specific conditions. Bioinformatics analyses of COPD datasets identified key modules and genes, which, together with AS-related targets from chemical databases, revealed 10 candidate genes. Machine learning further pinpointed 8 key genes (CDKN1A, F13A1, IL6, PLA2G2A, PTGS2, S100A8, SERPINE1, and THBS1), all significantly upregulated in COPD and enriched in pathways related to inflammation, immune response, and apoptosis. MR analysis confirmed that a causal link exists between the expression of CDKN1A, F13A1, IL6, and S100A8 in specific immune cells and COPD risk. title: Macrophage membrane-coated nanoparticles control pathological inflammation and enhance survival in models of severe bacterial pneumonia.
abstract: Rationale Severe bacterial pneumonia is a leading cause of death worldwide, and mortality rates remain unacceptably high despite appropriate antibiotic treatment. Macrophage membrane-coated nanoparticles (MΦ-NPs) are biomimetic constructs engineered to neutralize bacterial toxins, pathogen-associated molecular patterns, and proinflammatory cytokines. Objective To evaluate the therapeutic potential of MΦ-NPs for the treatment of severe bacterial pneumonia. Methods We evaluated the therapeutic potential of MΦ-NPs using in vitro models of infection involving human lung endothelial and epithelial cells, as well as primary human neutrophils, and in vivo murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia. Main results MΦ-NPs demonstrated potent cytoprotective and anti-inflammatory activity in vitro, without impairing neutrophil antimicrobial function. In both PA and MRSA pneumonia models, MΦ-NP treatment significantly improved survival, reduced bacterial burden, lowered proinflammatory cytokines, and preserved lung architecture. Quantitative proteomics further revealed suppression of inflammatory, coagulation, and fibrotic pathways associated with poor outcomes in human pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome. Conclusions These findings establish MΦ-NPs as a promising host-directed therapeutic strategy for mitigating the deleterious inflammatory sequelae of severe bacterial pneumonia.

title: <b><b>Safety profile and potential favorable reporting signals of liraglutide in patients with ulcerative colitis: A FAERS pharmacovigilance and network pharmacology study</b></b>.
abstract: Background Liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), has preclinical anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects, but its safety profile and potential favorable reporting associations in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain uncertain. Objectives To characterize liraglutide-associated reports in patients with UC and explore biological pathways that may contextualize the observed pharmacovigilance signals. Methods Reports submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2025, were analyzed in which liraglutide was recorded as the primary suspected drug and UC as the indication. Disproportionality was assessed using the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN) and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). Network pharmacology identified shared targets, constructed a protein-protein interaction network and performed Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses. Results Among 5,903 unique cases and 28,607 preferred-term event entries, the most frequent categories were general disorders and administration-site conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, injury or medication-related complications, infections and investigations. title: 2026 Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) strategy report: executive summary and key changes. From population evidence to personalized asthma care.
abstract: The Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) strategy report provides a comprehensive, annually updated evidence-based approach to asthma diagnosis, assessment, treatment, and prevention across the lifespan. Its central approach is personalized, iterative care based on the Assess-Adjust-Review cycle for both symptom control and reduction of future risk (including severe exacerbations, persistent airflow limitation, and treatment-related harm). GINA emphasizes objective confirmation of diagnosis wherever possible, and regular assessment of lung function, inhaler technique, adherence, multimorbidity, risk factors (including type 2 biomarkers), and patient goals and preferences. GINA strongly recommends that all adults, adolescents, children, and most preschoolers with asthma should receive inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing treatment. GINA recommends against short-acting β2-agonist (SABA)-only treatment. For adults/adolescents, GINA Track 1, using low-dose ICS-formoterol, an anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR), either as-needed-only or as maintenance-and-reliever therapy, is preferred because of its substantial reduction in severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based regimens, and its simplicity. Age-specific treatment pathways in children also emphasize ICS-containing therapy and exacerbation prevention. title: Incretins predict response to enteral nutrition strategies in the Early versus Delayed Enteral Nutrition trial: a secondary analysis.
abstract: Rationale The Early versus Delayed Enteral Nutrition (EDEN) trial found no significant difference in mortality between trophic and full enteral nutrition strategies in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. Heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) has been identified in prior ARDS trials. We previously identified intestine-derived incretin hormones (glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide [GIP] and glucagon-like peptide [GLP]-1) as potential predictive biomarkers in the response to nutrition. Objectives To investigate incretins as biomarkers predictive of HTE in EDEN. Methods Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, GLP-1, and host immune response biomarkers were measured from pre-intervention EDEN plasma samples. We investigated HTE with 60-day mortality as a primary outcome by testing interaction of treatment with circulating incretin levels in analyses adjusted for demographics, severity of illness, diabetes mellitus, and circulating IL-6 and assessed mortality by treatment arm across incretin tertiles. We additionally tested for HTE by de novo ARDS subphenotypes and by risk of mortality. Measurements and main results A total of 889 participants were included (452 randomly assigned to trophic and 437 to full enteral nutrition). title: Age-dependent remodeling of the peripheral nerve microenvironment: anatomical implications for perineural invasion
abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) involves interactions between malignant cells and the cellular and extracellular components of peripheral nerves. Although substantial evidence implicates Schwann cells, immune cells, and neurotrophic signaling in this process, the biological age of the invaded nerve has received limited attention. Peripheral nerves undergo age-related changes in Schwann-cell plasticity, inflammatory responses, and regenerative capacity, potentially altering the microenvironment encountered by invading tumor cells. We propose that peripheral nerve aging may influence PNI through changes in glial behavior, extracellular matrix organization, and the functional integrity of neural compartments. These mechanisms could have opposing effects: persistent inflammatory and senescence-associated signals might facilitate invasion, whereas reduced Schwann-cell plasticity might limit tumor-supportive repair programs. Current evidence does not establish which effect predominates. We outline an anatomically informed framework for investigating this hypothesis through age-comparative nerve models, compartment-specific histopathology, and spatial molecular profiling. Particular attention is given to the endoneurium, perineurium, and epineurium as distinct anatomical environments that may differentially influence tumor–nerve interactions. title: Lipid droplet dysmetabolism affects cell homeostasis in an in vitro model of Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Lipid droplets (LD) are dynamic organelles involved in neutral lipid storage, energy homeostasis, and protection against lipotoxicity and oxidative stress. Dysregulated LD metabolism has emerged as a pathological hallmark of several neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD). In this study, we investigated alterations in LD metabolism and their impact on mitochondria-associated membranes (MAM) using an in vitro AD model, namely mouse neuroblastoma N2A cells overexpressing the amyloid precursor protein carrying the familial Swedish mutation (APPswe). APPswe cells exhibited a marked depletion of LD accompanied by the accumulation of free fatty acids and triacylglycerol (TAG). These cells also displayed reduced levels of seipin, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and maintenance, potentially contributing to impaired TAG storage and LD formation. These lipid alterations were associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and lipid peroxidation, suggesting impaired stress buffering capacity. Pharmacological modulation of diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1), a key enzyme in TAG synthesis, was associated with an increase in LD size, improved endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria contacts, and enhanced mitochondrial function in APPswe cells. title: Leukocyte composition change persists through within-person differencing in ten-year blood methylation measures of aging
abstract: Longitudinal blood methylation measures of aging assume within-person differencing removes cellular heterogeneity, which requires composition to be time-invariant; in later life, it is not. In 86 participants of the Danish Longitudinal Study of Aging Twins sampled 10 years apart (Illumina 450 K, whole blood), we regressed 10-year change in four epigenetic clocks and a 48-locus methylation burden score on concurrent change in methylation-estimated leukocyte fractions. Composition change explained 11.5% (Horvath multi-tissue; permutation P = .13) to 41.2% (PhenoAge; P = 2 × 10 −4 ) of between-person variance, with adjusted R 2 of 0.05 to 0.37. The composition-associated shift in mean change, in standard deviations, was 0.13 (95% CI − 0.11 to 0.36) for the skin-and-blood clock, 0.15 (− 0.09 to 0.45) for Horvath, 0.40 (0.20 to 0.63) for Hannum, 0.45 (0.25 to 0.68) for the burden score, and 0.49 (0.30 to 0.74) for PhenoAge. PhenoAge was most composition-dependent under all three references, including one resolving naïve and memory subsets. title: Accelerometer-derived (timing of) physical activity and exercise in relation to incident osteoporosis in UK Biobank
abstract: Physical activity (PA) levels and timing may be essential for bone maintenance. We used large-scale prospective epidemiological cohort analyses to assess associations between accelerometer-derived (timing of) physical activity and incident osteoporosis risk. We included UK Biobank participants from the accelerometer substudy free of baseline osteoporosis. Data were processed centrally for determining overall acceleration, light intensity PA (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), as hourly and daily mean levels. K-means clustering was performed to identify groups with a similar circadian overall acceleration/LPA/MVPA timing pattern. Analyses between the different exposures with incident osteoporosis were conducted using multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. We included 93,928 participants (mean age 62.2 ± 7.9 years, 55.5% women). We observed that more overall acceleration, LPA and MVPA were associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis, with less time required in MVPA than LPA to reach similar risk reduction. Regarding timing, an acceleration pattern with a peak in the late morning associated with a 12% (HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.79–0.98) lower risk of incident osteoporosis compared to a broad midday peak. We observed no evidence for LPA timing effects. title: Ambient digital scribes in health care: a scoping review and evaluation checklist.
abstract: Clinical documentation is essential to quality care, although the shift to electronic health records has increased documentation burden, contributing to clinician burnout and workforce attrition. Ambient digital scribes (ADSs), artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled systems that passively capture clinician-patient encounters and automatically generate draft clinical notes, have been rapidly adopted across health systems as a potential solution. However, adoption has outpaced rigorous evaluation and existing guidance does not provide reporting standards that enable consistent assessment of ADSs across technical performance, clinical safety, equity, governance, and implementation domains. We conducted a scoping review to evaluate how ADS implementations are reported across technical performance, human oversight, sociotechnical implementation, and clinical outcomes and to identify reporting gaps to inform development of an evaluation framework. We included peer-reviewed, English-language empirical studies evaluating AI-enabled ambient documentation or scribing tools used by clinicians in simulated, hybrid, or real-world clinical settings and reporting quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods outcomes relevant to documentation or workflow. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase from database inception to Feb 10, 2026. We identified 52 studies published between 2023 and 2026. Most studies were observational or pilot implementations; only four randomised controlled
summary_short: Clinical documentation is essential to quality care, although the shift to electronic health records has increased documentation burden, contributing to clinician burnout and workforce attrition.

title: New technologies and cardiovascular longevity: From reactive cardiology to proactive longevity engineering.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and most clinical effort is still directed at disease that has already caused symptoms or events. Over the past decade, several technologies have made it possible to characterize cardiovascular risk and subclinical disease earlier and in more detail. This narrative review covers artificial intelligence applied to coronary CT angiography, cardiac MRI, and PET; coronary flow reserve; polygenic risk scores, lipoprotein(a), and proteomic and metabolomic panels; wearable and implantable monitoring; biosignal foundation models; digital twin models; biological aging clocks; and environmental exposures. We grade each against a three-level evidence hierarchy: whether the marker can be measured reliably, whether it adds prognostic information to standard risk assessment, and whether treatment guided by it improves outcomes compared with contemporary preventive care. Few markers have reached the third level. Coronary CT angiography reduced myocardial infarction in symptomatic patients in SCOT-HEART but did not improve outcomes compared with functional testing in PROMISE, and no randomized trial has tested treatment guided by AI-derived plaque metrics, polygenic scores, proteomic signatures, or aging clocks. Recent outcome trials of lipoprotein(a) lowering and interleukin-6 inhibition were neutral despite large changes in the target biomarkers. summary_short: Coronary CT angiography reduced myocardial infarction in symptomatic patients in SCOT-HEART but did not improve outcomes compared with functional testing in PROMISE, and no randomized trial has tested treatment guided by AI-derived plaque metrics, polygenic scores, proteomic signatures, or aging clocks.

title: Alcohol and cardiovascular healthspan: reappraising the evidence.
abstract: Healthy longevity is determined not only by how long we live, but by how long we remain free from the complications of chronic disease, disability, frailty, and impaired quality of life (QoL). Alcohol consumption is a potentially modifiable determinant of cardiovascular (CV) healthspan across the life course. Globally, alcohol use accounted for approximately 2.6 million deaths and 116 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 2019, while high alcohol use contributed 3.83 million CV DALYs in 2023, up from 2.86 million in 1990. Alcohol may adversely affect CV health through direct myocardial and vascular toxicity, as well as indirectly through an increased risk of developing hypertension and atrial fibrillation (AF), associations reported even at low-to-moderate levels of consumption in some studies, which may in turn contribute to major CV disease (CVD) events. Heavy alcohol exposure may lead to alcohol-induced cardiomyopathy (ACM), further compromising healthy longevity. Conversely, observational studies have suggested a J-shaped association between alcohol consumption and selected outcomes, particularly ischemic heart disease (IHD), with apparently lower risk among low-to-moderate drinkers. However, this apparent benefit is increasingly questioned by sick-quitter and healthy-user bias, residual confounding, reverse causality, and exposure misclassification. title: Cannabinoid Compounds in Binge Eating Disorder: From Neurobiological Mechanisms to Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Binge eating disorder (BED) is a prevalent but underrecognized psychiatric condition with limited mechanism-based therapies. The endocannabinoid system (ECS) critically regulates feeding and reward, making it a promising therapeutic target. This review aims to comprehensively evaluate the role of cannabinoid compounds (CCs) in BED, covering diagnostic criteria, pathogenesis, ECS dysregulation, classification of CCs, and preclinical/clinical evidence. This narrative review aims to comprehensively evaluate the role of cannabinoid compounds (CCs) in the treatment of BED, covering diagnostic criteria, pathogenesis, ECS regulation of feeding, classification of CCs, and preclinical and clinical evidence for cannabinoid-based interventions. A narrative synthesis was performed based on literature retrieved from eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP) and grey literature sources (ClinicalTrials.gov,WHO ICTRP, conference abstracts), without date or language restrictions. Preclinical animal studies, clinical trials, and mechanistic studies addressing CCs and binge-like eating were included. he ECS regulates food intake via central (hypothalamic-limbic) and peripheral (gut-brain vagal) pathways. In BED, ECS dysregulation manifests as intestinal CB1 overactivation suppressing CCK release, leptin resistance, and enhanced mesolimbic dopamine reward signaling. summary_short: Binge eating disorder (BED) is a prevalent but underrecognized psychiatric condition with limited mechanism-based therapies. The endocannabinoid system (ECS) critically regulates feeding and reward, making it a promising therapeutic target.

title: The Antipsychotic Pharmacological Target, GPR139, Engages Hypothalamic Spatiotemporal Signaling Without Promoting Metabolic Dysfunction.
abstract: Schizophrenia treatment remains limited to second-generation antipsychotics, which act as multi-target serotonin-dopamine receptor antagonists. Although effective against positive symptoms, their broader antagonism at 5-HT2C, H1 and muscarinic receptors drives weight gain, with limited benefit for negative and cognitive symptoms. Here, we characterize the orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR139, a predominantly CNS-expressed receptor as a potential pharmacological target in schizophrenia, and explore the metabolic effects of its activation. Molecular docking showed that TAK-041, a GPR139 agonist, binds the GPR139 orthosteric pocket, overlapping with predicted aromatic amino acid ligand-binding poses. In hypothalamic mHypoE-N39 cells, BRET assays revealed preferential Gαq and Gαi coupling, alongside detectable Gαs recruitment, PLC-dependent cAMP elevation, and Gαi-mediated inhibitory modulation of cAMP production. Compartmentalized BRET assays further revealed time-dependent responses associated with distinct intracellular compartment markers, including Gαs responses associated with recycling endosome markers. HILO microscopy revealed changes in the distribution of GPR139-YFP fluorescence following TAK-041 stimulation. In vivo, chronic TAK-041 administration to chow-fed mice improved insulin sensitivity without significant changes in cumulative food intake or body composition. title: Dietary Fiber-Derived Short-Chain Fatty Acids as Critical Intermediates of the Gut Microbiome in Metabolic Health and Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia due to impaired insulin secretion or action. Even with significant progress in medications, diabetes still creates a major global health burden because of its increasing prevalence and related complications. Recent studies highlight the crucial role of gut microbes and their microbial metabolites, especially short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), in regulating blood sugar levels, insulin sensitivity, inflammation, and energy balance in T2DM. Thus, this review aims to critically examine the role of gut microbiota-derived SCFAs, such as acetate, propionate, and butyrate, in T2DM pathophysiology and management, with a primary focus on their molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential through dietary, microbiome-targeted, and SCFA-based interventions. SCFAs, including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, accumulate due to fermentation of dietary fibers by gut bacteria. Functionally, these microbial metabolites serve as important signaling molecules that affect the host's metabolism through various mechanisms, including activation of G-protein-coupled receptor 41 (GPR41; also known as free fatty acid receptor 3, FFAR3) and GPR43 (FFAR2), and modulation of gut hormone secretion like Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and Peptide YY (PYY). It also helps in managing immune responses and epigenetic regulation through histone deacetylase inhibition. In conclusion, SCFAs link the gut microbiome with h
summary_short: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia due to impaired insulin secretion or action. Even with significant progress in medications, diabetes still creates a major global health burden because of its increasing prevalence and related complications.

title: Update on the role of bariatric endoscopy in the era of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual incretin agonists have transformed obesity care. This review summarizes recent advances in endoscopic bariatric and metabolic therapies (EBMTs) and examines their evolving role alongside incretin-based pharmacotherapy. Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) has become the most established primary endoscopic bariatric therapy, with durable weight loss now shown through 5 years. Newer approaches target physiology rather than gastric volume: gastric fundal mucosal ablation lowers ghrelin and hunger, duodenal mucosal resurfacing has shown modest benefit over sham, and magnetic duodeno-ileostomy is an emerging intestinal option. Predominantly observational data suggest that combining EBMTs with GLP-1 RAs, particularly when pharmacotherapy is started after the procedure, yields greater weight loss than either alone. Comparative studies indicate that the two approaches are not interchangeable, and early phenotyping data suggest that satiation-based markers may predict response to both. EBMTs and GLP-1 RAs are complementary rather than competing therapies. Randomized trials are needed to define optimal sequencing, tolerability and durability, and to test whether phenotype-guided selection can individualize multimodal obesity care.

title: Pharmacotherapy for Alcohol Use Disorder: Current Evidence and Clinical Perspectives.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a leading preventable cause of morbidity and mortality, yet evidence-based pharmacotherapy remains underused. This structured narrative review evaluates established, off-label, Europe-specific, and emerging pharmacological treatments for AUD, with emphasis on treatment goals, patient selection, safety, comorbidity, and regulatory context. In our narrative synthesis, acamprosate and oral naltrexone are the best-supported first-line options, consistent with the formal moderate-strength evidence ratings reported in the 2023 Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) systematic review and meta-analysis; they serve different clinical objectives, with acamprosate better supported for maintaining abstinence after detoxification and naltrexone for reducing heavy drinking and limiting escalation after a lapse. Supervised disulfiram remains relevant for highly motivated patients pursuing abstinence. Nalmefene, sodium oxybate, and baclofen illustrate the heterogeneity of European practice and the need to balance efficacy, tolerability, misuse liability, and authorization status. Among off-label agents, topiramate has moderate-strength evidence for several continuous drinking outcomes, although cognitive and sensory adverse effects limit acceptability; gabapentin may be useful when insomnia, anxiety, or protracted withdrawal symptoms are prominent, but aggregate evidence is of lower certainty. title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist treatment and bariatric surgery for the management of early-onset, severe obesity associated with two homozygous melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) variants: a case report.
abstract: Biallelic, (likely) pathogenic germline variants in the melanocortin 4 receptor gene (MC4R) that impair protein function and disrupt the leptin-melanocortin pathway, lead to impaired satiety and hyperphagia, causing early-onset severe obesity. Weight management in affected individuals is challenging since behavioral interventions are not effective. We report on a female adolescent with severe obesity associated with the two homozygous, (likely) pathogenic variants MC4R:c.253 A > G;p.(Ser85Gly) and MC4R:c.802T > C;p.(Tyr268His). She was referred to our specialized genetic obesity clinic with a request for bariatric surgery. The patient had numerous prior weight loss attempts without success. Her weight at admission was 200.8 kg (body mass index [BMI] 75.2 kg/m2). Diagnostic investigations revealed impaired fasting glucose, dyslipidemia, hyperuricemia, and elevated transaminases, along with severe obstructive sleep apnea with hypoventilation syndrome and arterial hypertension. In addition, she had a post-traumatic stress disorder. We followed a combined treatment regime comprising pharmacotherapy with the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist, liraglutide, and sleeve gastrectomy coupled with a multidisciplinary pre-and post-surgery intervention program. This patient-tailored treatment induced significant weight loss at the last follow-up 12 months after surgery with partial improvement of the comorbidities. A transient prerenal acute kidney injury was observed due to insuffic
summary_short: We report on a female adolescent with severe obesity associated with the two homozygous, (likely) pathogenic variants MC4R:c.253 A > G;p.(Ser85Gly) and MC4R:c.802T > C;p.(Tyr268His).

title: Dulaglutide inhibits atrial steatosis and atrial fibrillation in transgenic mice with cardiac-specific perilipin 2-overexpression.
abstract: Patients with diabetes and obesity are prone to developing atrial fibrillation (AF) and myocardial steatosis, which leads to intracellular lipotoxicity. We investigated the effects of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide on atrial lipid accumulation and AF in cardiac-specific perilipin 2-overexpressing mice (PLIN2-Tg). Dulaglutide (0.5 mg/kg) or saline was administered every four days for 8 weeks to wild-type (WT) and PLIN2-Tg mice. Atrial lipid accumulation, electrophysiological parameters, and oxidative stress were evaluated after treatment. PLIN2-Tg mice showed increased atrial lipid accumulation and greater AF inducibility and duration compared with WT mice. Although circulating free fatty acid levels were unchanged, dulaglutide treatment was associated with lower atrial triacylglycerol content and lipid droplet accumulation. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels were significantly lower in dulaglutide-treated PLIN2-Tg mice than in saline-treated PLIN2-Tg mice. In addition, dulaglutide suppressed AF frequency and duration and improved atrial conduction velocity. These findings suggest that dulaglutide treatment is associated with lower atrial lipid accumulation and mitochondrial oxidative stress, together with an improvement in the electrophysiological phenotype of PLIN2-Tg mice. Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying these associations.

title: Spatially Organized Core-Shell Microcapsules Harness Epidermal-Dermal Coupling for Anti-Photoaging Therapy.
abstract: Skin aging involves concurrent epidermal barrier dysfunction and dermal metabolic decline, yet current interventions largely neglect functional coupling between these layers. Herein, a core-shell microcapsule system (SA@B@Lips) is designed for spatially organized and sustained delivery. Specifically, SA@B@Lips supports prolonged probiotic confinement under the tested in vitro conditions, while Dil-associated fluorescence indicates the deeper skin penetration of NMN-loaded liposomes. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis implicates transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/SMAD-related signaling in the epidermal response, while Wnt/β-catenin- and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)-related signaling emerges as candidate pathways associated with the response of dermal fibroblasts to NMN. These transcriptomic findings provide potential mechanistic insights into the coordinated epidermal-dermal interaction associated with collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix remodeling. In UVB-induced photoaging models, SA@B@Lips reduces epidermal hyperplasia to approximately 20.4 µm, promotes dermal collagen reorganization, and increases skin elasticity by approximately 2.3-fold, outperforming single-component treatments. Beyond local tissue repair, SA@B@Lips attenuates peripheral inflammation and supports epidermal immune homeostasis, while concurrent changes in the skin and gut microbiota are consistent with a possible skin-gut association. title: Adjunctive nutraceuticals in early psychosis: an updated systematic review of efficacy and tolerability.
abstract: Supplemental nutraceuticals have shown promise as augmentation strategies in psychotic disorders and potentially target different physiological pathways to standard antipsychotic medications. This systematic review aimed to update a 2017 review examining evidence from clinical trials on the efficacy and tolerability of adjunctive nutraceuticals in early psychosis, and exploring potential mechanisms of action based on neurobiological outcomes reported in the included trials. Publications reporting quantitative outcomes from adjunctive nutraceutical trials in early psychosis were eligible for inclusion. A systematic search of seven psychiatric and clinical trials databases was conducted for new publications until December 2025. Data were extracted and organised according to each class of nutraceutical identified. Studies were assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool and limitations were included in a narrative synthesis of the findings. After screening 1,739 unique reports, sixteen were eligible and are presented alongside the eleven articles from the original review. These 27 articles stem from fifteen randomised trials and include a total of 1,006 individuals. Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (k=13) and N-acetylcysteine (k=6) were the most widely studied agents, with some trials reporting improvements in general psychopathology and negative symptoms, while neurobiological findings suggest plausible antioxidant and neuroprotective mechanisms. title: Latest Concepts in Meniscal Allograft Transplantation.
abstract: Meniscal allograft transplantation has evolved to a standard-of-care procedure for selected symptomatic patients with meniscal deficiency. Clinical success is highly dependent on rigorous patient selection and optimization of the joint environment, often necessitating concomitant procedures such as anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction or corrective osteotomies to ensure graft longevity. Although bony fixation techniques have traditionally been considered the biomechanical gold standard, soft-tissue fixation techniques demonstrate comparable clinical outcomes. Long-term data suggest that meniscal allograft transplantation is a durable intervention, with 10-year survivorship rates ranging from 73.5% to 85%. Recent progress in areas such as synthetic grafts, artificial intelligence for preoperative planning, and three-dimensional bioprinted scaffolds could further improve outcomes and potentially decrease or even eliminate the dependence on cadaver grafts. However, much further development is required before these technologies are fully realized.

title: Social comparison via physical activity leaderboards: perceptions, preferences, and implications for physical activity promotion among insufficiently active adults.
abstract: Social comparison is often used to promote physical activity (PA; e.g., via leaderboards that rank users' PA behavior), but their utility among insufficiently active adults is unclear. Our aim was to describe these adults' perceptions of social comparison, broadly and in the context of PA leaderboards. Participants (N = 21; M Age = 36 years; M BMI = 30.5 kg/m 2 ; 33% men; 62% from underrepresented groups in the United States) completed a survey and a semi-structured interview; they described their perceptions of social comparison and leaderboards and their reactions to images of a PA leaderboard interface. We used reflexive thematic analysis with member checking to generate and refine five themes: (1) a shift in overall attitudes toward comparison (from negative to neutral/mixed); (2) responses depend on person-level traits and situational factors; (3) even without context, leaderboards prompt emotional responses; (4) openness to PA leaderboards for motivating PA; and (5) desire for ways to connect with others around PA. Although comparison was initially perceived as negative, leaderboards were described positively. We present potential explanations for this discrepancy-including perceptions of distinct purposes for leaderboards versus comparison more broadly-as well as considerations for future work. Overall, findings suggest the potential acceptability of leaderboards to support PA promotion among insufficiently active adults, and their effects on PA motivation and behavior

title: Millennial-Scale Persistence and Long-Term Dormancy of Bloom-Forming Cyanobacteria in the Baltic Sea Revealed by Viable Resting Stages and Sedimentary Ancient DNA.
abstract: Blooms of filamentous diazotrophic cyanobacteria (Nostocales) have occurred in the Baltic Sea for millennia but are expected to intensify under ongoing climate warming and eutrophication, with consequences for ecosystem health. Nostocales form resting stages (akinetes) that are preserved in sediments, enabling reconstruction of past bloom dynamics. We investigated past and contemporary variability in the abundance of bloom-forming Nostocales by analysing akinetes and sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) metabarcoding from central Baltic Sea sediments, spanning ~7200 calibrated years before present (cal yr BP). Akinete viability was assessed by dead-cell staining and fluorescence microscopy. Akinetes were present back to ~3580 cal yr BP, with 98% remaining viable for up to 200 years and the oldest viable akinete persisting up to ~1450 years, highlighting resilience in hypoxic Baltic Sea sediments. SedaDNA extended the Nostocales record back to ~7150 cal yr BP. Both parameters showed a significant increase in Nostocales abundance since the 1990s, likely driven by past anthropogenic nutrient inputs before and ongoing climate warming in the Baltic Sea. The findings highlight the value of a multi-parameter approach, while discrepancies between akinete and sedaDNA records underscore the complexity of reconstructing past cyanobacterial abundance from sedimentary archives.
summary_short: SedaDNA extended the Nostocales record back to ~7150 cal yr BP.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Middle-Aged and Older Adults in Korea: Applying the AWGS 2025.
abstract: Background This study examined sarcopenia prevalence and explored associated factors among community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults in Korea using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 criteria. Methods We analysed 5600 adults aged 50-80 years from the 2022 and 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys (KNHANES) and 2401 older adults aged 70-84 years from the 2016-2017 baseline of the Korean Frailty and Aging Cohort Study (KFACS). Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) were used to measure appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM). Age-group-specific contributors to sarcopenia were identified using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAPs) with temporal validation. Results In the KNHANES dataset, the mean age was 57.3 ± 4.4 years among middle-aged adults (50-64 years) and 72.6 ± 5.1 years among older adults ≥ 65 years. According to AWGS 2025 criteria, prevalence of possible sarcopenia, height-adjusted sarcopenia (ASM/height 2 + grip strength) and BMI-adjusted sarcopenia (ASM/BMI + grip strength) was 11.2%, 5.6% and 6.3% in middle-aged adults and 14.5%, 9.1% and 10.2% in older adults ≥ 65 years, respectively. Height-adjusted sarcopenia was more common in men among middle-aged adults but did not differ significantly by sex in older adults (p > 0.05). title: Sex-Specific Myostatin-Grey Matter Volume Associations in Ageing Adults: Implications for the Muscle-Brain Axis.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cognitive decline, suggesting bidirectional muscle-brain crosstalk mediated by myokines. Myostatin, a negative regulator of muscle growth, may influence brain health through systemic signalling, yet human neuroimaging evidence remains lacking. Moreover, men and women exhibit distinct patterns of muscle ageing and cognitive decline, but sex-specific effects of myostatin on brain structure have not been investigated. This study examined associations between serum myostatin and regional brain grey matter volume (GMV) in ageing adults, with emphasis on sexual dimorphism. Methods We analysed 482 community-dwelling participants (235 males, 247 females; mean age 67.2 ± 8.5 years, range of 50-88) from the I-Lan Longitudinal Aging Study. Serum myostatin levels, muscle mass and grip strength were assessed. High-resolution brain MRI was processed using voxel-based morphometry to examine associations between myostatin and regional GMV. title: Why Anthropologists Should Study Dogs.
abstract: While primates have traditionally been a focus of evolutionary anthropologists, the domestic dog represents a valuable complementary model due to its long shared evolutionary history with humans. The advantages of studying dogs are particularly evident in four key areas: (1) analyzing evolutionary adaptations, (2) understanding humanity's past, (3) examining humanity's cultural diversity, and (4) assessing factors that influence human health. Dogs have convergently evolved social cognition and local adaptations (including altitude adaptations and the ability to digest starches and lactose) that parallel those of humans, making them valuable models for testing evolutionary hypotheses. The global spread of dogs also illuminates human population histories, and isotopic analyses of dog remains can be proxies for human dietary data when sampling human remains is infeasible or inappropriate. Dogs' near-universal presence across human societies and exposure to the same real-world environments further make them uniquely powerful models for studying cultural variation and health.

title: Targeted modulation of protein post-translational modifications through induced proximity: advances and practical toolkits.
abstract: Targeted post-translational modification (PTM) of a protein of interest (POI) is achieved by inducing proximity to a protein-modifying effector enzyme in cells. A number of distinct induced proximity modalities, including genetically encodable polypeptides, small heterobifunctional molecules and molecular glues, can be applied to induce proximity between virtually any two intracellular proteins. Because targeted PTM can alter protein function and fate, induced proximity offers a route to target many proteins previously considered undruggable. With several molecular glue degraders long employed in clinic and one proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) recently FDA-approved for clinical use, induced proximity modality has emerged as clinically validated and rapidly expanding avenue for drug discovery. Beyond therapeutic applications, targeted PTM provides a versatile experimental platform for dissecting the functions and consequences of specific PTMs in physiological and disease contexts. In this review, we present an up-to-date overview of advances in targeted modulation of protein PTMs using induced-proximity technologies. We also highlight several induced-proximity toolkits and include practical information on them to facilitate their rapid adoption for proof-of-concept studies on targeted modulation of PTMs in cells.

title: Astragaloside IV and Ferroptosis Modulation in Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy: Current Evidence, an Integrative Hypothesis, and Future Directions.
abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is initially an adaptive response to sustained mechanical, neurohormonal, or metabolic stress; however, it can progress to fibrosis, contractile dysfunction, arrhythmia, and heart failure. Ferroptosis is a type of regulated cell death caused by iron-dependent phospholipid peroxidation. Evidence consistent with ferroptosis, such as disrupted iron homeostasis, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired antioxidant defense, has been reported in experimental models of pathological cardiac hypertrophy; however, these findings do not by themselves establish ferroptosis as a cause of hypertrophic remodeling. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) is a cycloartane-type triterpene saponin from Astragalus species that has shown anti-hypertrophic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, metabolic-regulatory and mitochondrial-protective effects in experimental cardiovascular models. AS-IV has also shown anti-ferroptotic effects in several cardiac and extra-cardiac disease models by means of Nrf2-centred antioxidant defense, regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4, p53 signaling, CD36-dependent lipid handling, and 14-3-3η-linked regulation of GPX4 stability. Nevertheless, whether ferroptosis inhibition directly contributes to the anti-hypertrophic effect of AS-IV in pathological cardiac hypertrophy remains unproven because direct causal validation in dedicated hypertrophy models is lacking. Ferroptosis is a type of regulated cell death caused by iron-dependent phospholipid peroxidation.

title: Impacts of Retrospective Lipid Suppression on Metabolite Quantification in Preclinical Proton MR Spectroscopic Imaging.
abstract: Extracranial lipid contamination remains a challenge in proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI), especially in short acquisition delay MRSI, where broad lipid resonances overlap with metabolite and macromolecular signals. Although retrospective lipid suppression techniques are widely used in human MRSI, their effects on metabolite quantification in preclinical MRSI, which is more prone to lipid contamination, have not yet been examined. In this study, we assessed how the retrospective lipid suppression and spectral fitting range influence spectral quality, spatial metabolite mapping, and quantification variability using proton MRSI of rat brains at 14.1 T. Lipid suppression was applied via an orthogonal projection method to both fully sampled and compressed sensing datasets, each comprising data with minimal and pronounced lipid contamination. Spectral fitting was performed with both broad (4.1-0.2 ppm) and narrow (4.1-1.8 ppm) ranges. When lipid contamination was minimal, suppression caused only slight spectral and spatial changes, with consistent metabolite quantification across conditions. In contrast, datasets with pronounced lipid contamination exhibited notable spectral changes following suppression, consequently affecting spatial metabolite mapping and concentration estimates. title: Separation of Anatomical Contributions in MRSI Using a Non-Negative Geographically Weighted Regression Model.
abstract: Magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) is a non-invasive neuroimaging tool that maps brain metabolites, providing insights into brain physiology and pathology. However, clinical adoption remains limited due to low spatial resolution and partial volume effects, where acquired signals detect metabolism from different tissue types, preventing clear identification of tissue-specific metabolic patterns. We developed a statistical framework based on non-negative geographically weighted regression (NNGWR) designed to overcome these limitations. The method integrates tissue partial volumes with MRSI data using spatially adaptive regression to interpolate metabolite levels across the imaging volume while separating distinct tissue contributions. Importantly, our model accounts for spatial heterogeneity within tissues rather than assuming metabolic uniformity, providing more physiologically realistic estimates. Simulations using synthetic ground truth data show that our method consistently achieves a lower median absolute percentage error than cubic spline and zero-filling interpolations, especially under high noise or low-resolution conditions. A total of 120 MRSI datasets were acquired at 3 T from a cohort of 36 healthy volunteers to assess predictive performance. title: Associations between fruit, vegetable and fish and epigenetic markers of ageing and protein EpiScores in Generation Scotland
abstract: Consumption of foods such as fruit, vegetables and fish has been associated with a reduced risk of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and greater longevity. These effects could, at least in part, be underpinned by epigenetic alterations, including changes in DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. The aim of the current study was to characterise cross-sectional associations between three selected food components (fruit, vegetables and fish) and measures of DNA methylation associated with biological ageing (DNAm PhenoAge, DNAm GrimAge and DNAm Telomere Length), and epigenetic scores—or EpiScores—for 109 proteins in Generation Scotland. This study used dietary data collected on frequency and consumption quantities of fresh fruit ( n = 8648), vegetables ( n = 8686) and fish ( n = 5070). Linear regression models were used to test associations between food components and DNAm GrimAge, DNAm PhenoAge, DNAm Telomere Length, DNAm IL6 and the 109 EpiScores), After correction for multiple testing, there were several significant associations between food and the epigenetic biomarkers.. These findings provide additional evidence that dietary behaviours are associated with DNA methylation-derived biomarkers of ageing and health. Future research could focus on external validation of our results, and use longitudinal data to explore causal pathways.

title: Adropin ameliorates endometrial defects in letrozole induced hyperandrogenic mice.
abstract: Hyperandrogenism, a hallmark feature of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is associated with endometrial dysfunction. Adropin, a hepatokine, has been reported to restore reproductive activity in PCOS mice. However, its role in uterine physiology remains elusive. Hence, the present study was undertaken to elucidate the effects of exogenous adropin treatment on endometrial functions in letrozole-induced hyperandrogenic (HA) mouse. Letrozole (6 mg/kg body weight) was given orally for 21 days to induce hyperandrogenism in female mouse. Thereafter, intraperitoneal injection of adropin (450 nmol/kg body weight) was given to HA mouse for 15 days. Decreased expression of adropin and its receptor GPR19 was observed in the uterus of HA mouse compared to vehicle control. Administration of adropin to HA mouse significantly reduced the uterine testosterone level while increasing the estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) levels. These hormonal changes were associated with enhanced proliferation of luminal and glandular epithelial cells (LE and GE) and an increased number of endometrial glands compared with HA mouse uterus. title: Spermidine improves fast-twitch muscle histopathology and specific-force, and select bone properties, in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), an X-linked recessive disease, primarily affects skeletal and cardiac muscle, leading to progressive muscle wasting and weakness, but is also associated with compromised bone quality and microstructure. Human and mdx mouse studies show that DMD is associated with impaired muscle autophagy. The polyamine, spermidine, is known to stimulate autophagy, which some studies have linked to the upregulation of the microtubule-associated MAP1S protein. Spermidine has been shown to improve aspects of collagen VI deficiency-induced myopathy, in part, by reactivating autophagy. Thus, it was hypothesized that spermidine supplementation would improve the muscle pathology of DMD mdx mice, which would be associated with enhanced markers of autophagy and MAP1S. The impact of spermidine on bone quality or microstructure was also assessed using Synchrotron-generated x-ray imaging and 3-point bending. Three-week-old wild type (WT) and mdx mice were supplemented with 3 mM spermidine in drinking water for 13 weeks. Spermidine had no impact on mdx slow-twitch soleus muscle histopathology or contractile function, but improved mdx fast-twitch EDL muscle mass and specific tetanic force, which was associated with reduced centrally localized nuclei and tissue infiltrate. Surprisingly, despite a spermidine-induced increase in MAP1S protein, there was no change in markers of autophagy or autophagic flux. title: Host preference and larval performance of <i>Eueides isabella dianasa</i> (Hübner, 1806) (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae: Heliconiinae) on <i>Passiflora</i> spp. (Malpighiales: Passifloraceae).
abstract: Passion fruit crops ( Passiflora spp.) are affected by several insect pests, including defoliating caterpillars such as Eueides isabella dianasa (Hübner, 1806) (Nymphalidae: Heliconiinae), a Neotropical butterfly distributed from the United States and Mexico to southern Brazil, whose larvae feed on multiple Passiflora species. Understanding plant-insect interactions through host preference and suitability is essential for supporting effective pest management. Therefore, the objectives of this study were (i) to evaluate host preference and leaf consumption of E. i. dianasa on different Passiflora species and (ii) to compare its developmental performance and survival on these hosts. Overall, Passiflora alata Curtis and Passiflora cincinnata Mast. showed lower host preference, whereas Passiflora edulis Sims was the most attractive host for E. i. dianasa at 3 and 10 days of larval age. Leaf consumption differed significantly among the Passiflora species, with P. edulis showing the highest consumption (95.15%), followed by P. cincinnata (24.54%) and P. alata (0.70%). Regarding developmental performance, host plant species did not affect the duration or weight of the larval and pupal stages. However, significant effects were observed on larval survival, larval and pupal viability, and adult longevity. title: From GLP-1 Receptor Agonism to Multi-Receptor Targeting in Kidney Disease.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are established kidney-protective therapy in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease, and co-agonists and multi-agonists that also target the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon receptors are advancing. Most reviews address these agents as a single class. This narrative review examines the three receptors separately, distinguishing the renal efficacy of a molecule from the causal contribution attributable to each of its receptor targets, and addresses three questions. First, what is known about the renal actions of each receptor: GLP-1 receptor agonism is the only receptor profile for which a drug (semaglutide) has shown kidney benefit in a dedicated outcome trial (FLOW), although the receptor-specific mechanism in humans is not established, as natriuresis is acute, not sustained, and hemodynamic effects are context-dependent; no GIP receptor-specific renal signature has been established in humans; and glucagon receptor signaling appears bidirectional, with potentially protective tubular actions coexisting with a risk of hyperfiltration. title: Effects of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 on Inflammation-Related Gene Expression in Adipose Tissue of Women with Obesity.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is known to have anti-inflammatory activity; however, its effects on the chronic low-grade inflammation present in the adipose tissue of individuals with obesity remain unclear. This study investigated the effect of GLP-1 infusion on inflammation related gene expression in the adipose tissue of women with obesity. Eleven women with obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m 2 ), aged 28-63 years, participated in a single blind, randomized, crossover study comparing 4 h infusions of synthetic human GLP-1 (7- 36) at 0.9 pmol/kg/min and saline after an overnight fasting. Total RNA was isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies collected before and immediately after each infusion. Expression of 249 inflammation-related genes from the Human Inflammation Panel was assessed. Compared with saline infusion, an approximately two-fold increase in circulating GLP-1 induced by GLP-1 infusion significantly downregulated the expression of the pro-inflammatory genes TNF , C2 , CD4 , and MAPKAPK2 during the fasting state, with a near-significant reduction in MMP9 and IL8 expression. Upregulation of the anti-inflammatory regulator TOLLIP was also observed. Collectively, these results indicate an anti-inflammatory effect of GLP-1. Additionally, MAP2K1 , MAP2K4 , RIPK2 , and PLA2G4A , genes involved in adipose tissue remodeling, were upregulated during GLP-1 infusion. MCOLN1/TRPML1 regulates lysosomal acidification through Ca<sup>2+</sup>-CAMK2/CaMKII-DMXL1-mediated V-ATPase assembly in cellular and mouse models of Alzheimer disease.
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline and amyloid beta (Aβ) pathology, with emerging evidence indicating that autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction acts as an early pathogenic event. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes remain incompletely understood. This study demonstrated that MCOLN1/TRPML1 (mucolipin TRP cation channel 1), a lysosomal Ca 2+ channel, was consistently downregulated in the hippocampus of patients with AD, five familial Alzheimer disease mutations (5xFAD) mice, and neuroblastoma Neuro-2a cells stably expressing human APP695 (N2a-APP) cells. Knockdown of Mcoln1 specifically in the hippocampus of mice recapitulated key AD-related phenotypes, including impaired lysosomal acidification, defective autophagic degradation, lysosomal enlargement, Aβ accumulation, dendritic spine loss, and cognitive deficits. Conversely, pharmacological activation with Mucolipin synthetic agonist 1 (ML-SA1) or genetic overexpression of MCOLN1 alleviated these abnormalities and mitigated Aβ pathology and cognitive impairments in 5xFAD mice. Mechanistically, decreased MCOLN1 protein impaired the vacuolar H + -ATPase (V-ATPase) assembly, potentially via diminished DMXL1 (Dmx like 1) phosphorylation through the Ca 2+ -CAMK2/CaMKII (calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase II) signaling pathway. title: Dietary selenium deficiency causes insulin-like growth factor 1 resistance in skeletal muscle of zebrafish.
abstract: Selenium (Se), an essential trace element for humans and animals, is critical for skeletal muscle homeostasis. Its deficiency is associated with low muscle mass due to the inhibition of the target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1)-mediated protein synthesis. However, the mechanism by which dietary Se deficiency hinders TORC1-mediated muscle protein synthesis remains unclear. Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1), a key upstream signaling molecule for TORC1, is pivotal in regulating muscle protein synthesis. This study evaluated whether dietary Se deficiency affects the transduction and transmission of IGF1 signaling in skeletal muscle using a zebrafish model, by manipulating dietary Se levels with Se-enriched yeast. Strikingly, dietary Se deficiency induced marked IGF1 resistance in skeletal muscle, characterized by elevated tissue IGF1 level but impaired transduction of both endogenous and exogenous IGF1 signaling from membrane receptor (IGF1 receptor/insulin receptor) to intracellular insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1). Mechanistically, dietary Se deficiency downregulated numerous antioxidant selenoproteins, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, activated the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), and increased the phosphorylation of IRS1 at Ser 307 and Ser 312 sites, suggesting involvement of the ROS-mediated JNK-IRS1 pathway in dietary Se deficiency-induced IGF1 resistance. title: Dose optimization study of hydroxychloroquine as add-on therapy in patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus.
abstract: Objective Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is approved in India as third-line therapy for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) at a recommended daily dose of 400 mg. However, concerns regarding cumulative retinal toxicity with long-term use highlight the need to identify the lowest effective dose. This study evaluated the efficacy and short-term safety of HCQ 200 mg, 300 mg, and 400 mg once daily in patients with inadequately controlled T2DM. Methods In this randomized, double-blind, multicentre dose-optimization trial, adults with inadequately controlled T2DM despite stable metformin and sulfonylurea therapy were randomized to receive HCQ 200 mg, 300 mg, or 400 mg once daily for 24 weeks. Efficacy endpoints included changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting, postprandial glucose, and lipid parameters at Weeks 12 and 24. Safety was assessed through adverse-event, laboratory investigations, and ophthalmologic evaluations. Results Overall, 218 participants were randomized (mean age 48.22 ± 8.86 years; 58.7% male). At Week 24, mean HbA1c reductions from baseline were -0.64%, -0.78%, and -0.89% in the 200 mg, 300 mg, and 400 mg groups, respectively. Lipid parameters improved across groups. Sixteen participants experienced 23 adverse events; of which 82.6% unrelated to study medication. One serious adverse event, unrelated to HCQ, resolved without sequelae. No retinal abnormalities or ophthalmic adverse events were observed. Conclusion HCQ 200 mg, 300 mg, and 400 mg demonstrated clinica

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Reveals Altitude-Associated Molecular Responses in the Honey Bee (<i>Apis mellifera</i>).
abstract: Honey bees inhabit a broad range of elevations, yet how they adjust physiologically and molecularly to high-altitude environments remains incompletely understood. Here, we compared the thoracic transcriptomes and proteomes of Apis mellifera populations collected from high- and low-altitude sites in Tibet. In high-altitude bees, transcriptional changes were mainly associated with oxidative phosphorylation, the citrate cycle, pyruvate metabolism, thermogenesis, cardiac muscle contraction, and motor proteins, indicating prominent changes in pathways related to energy metabolism and muscle-related functions. In contrast, genes associated with longevity regulation were predominantly downregulated. Proteomic differences were mainly concentrated in metabolic pathways. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further revealed increased expression of immune-related molecules in high-altitude bees. Because immune activity is energetically costly, this response may represent an additional component of the energetic investment required for high-altitude adaptation. The coordinated molecular changes in energy metabolism, muscle function, and immune activity may help honey bees maintain physiological performance under high-altitude conditions, while the downregulation of longevity-associated pathways may reflect trade-offs in resource allocation and somatic maintenance. These results highlight the coordinated molecular adjustments underlying honey bee responses to high-altitude env
