title: Electro-oxidative treatment of municipal sludge: a sustainable approach for bacterial control.
abstract: This study evaluated electrooxidation (EO) using mixed metal oxide (MMO) anodes for stabilizing and disinfecting waste-activated sludge. Batch experiments took place at current densities of 7.14 to 11.90 mA cm -2 with 1.25 g per L NaCl for 10 minutes. Under optimized conditions, EO achieved over 99.9% bacterial inactivation along with significant reductions in organic load, including about 45% COD, 51% BOD, and 27% TOC removal. Nutrient transformation occurred, with about 96% phosphorus reduction and increased soluble nitrogen species due to mineralization. EO treatment also lowered odorous gas emissions; H 2 S and NH 3 concentrations decreased from 10.18 to 2.99 mg L -1 and from 9.04 to 1.55 mg L -1 , respectively. The MMO anodes showed high stability with minimal compositional changes after 50 cycles. The treated sludge remained suitable for vermicomposting, confirming its compatibility with downstream biological processes. These findings indicate that EO offers a fast and effective pretreatment strategy for improving sludge stability, biosafety, and resource recovery potential.
summary_short: Nutrient transformation occurred, with about 96% phosphorus reduction and increased soluble nitrogen species due to mineralization. These findings indicate that EO offers a fast and effective pretreatment strategy for improving sludge stability, biosafety, and resource recovery potential.

title: Biomass-derived biochar as a sustainable catalyst support for fuel desulfurization: a critical review of adsorptive and oxidative pathways toward ultra-low-sulfur fuels.
abstract: Sulfur-containing compounds in transportation fuels remain a major environmental and industrial challenge because they generate SO x emissions, accelerate refinery corrosion, poison catalytic converters, and contribute to atmospheric pollution. Despite the fact that hydrodesulfurization (HDS) remains the dominant industrial desulfurization technology, its limited effectiveness toward sterically hindered sulfur compounds, particularly alkylated dibenzothiophenes such as 4,6-dimethyldibenzothiophene (4,6-DMDBT), has intensified the search for alternative deep-desulfurization technologies operating under mild conditions. Among these, adsorptive desulfurization (ADS) and oxidative desulfurization (ODS) have emerged as the most promising approaches, in which the physicochemical properties of the adsorbent or catalyst support largely determine the sulfur-removal efficiency. This review presents the first comprehensive and systematic comparison of biochar with conventional desulfurization materials, including γ-Al 2 O 3 , SiO 2 , and activated carbon, across both ADS and ODS systems. Beyond summarizing recent advances, this review establishes a unified mechanistic framework linking biochar's structure to its catalytic and adsorptive performance. title: Retrospective Observational Study of Kaposi Sarcoma.
abstract: Background Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is a human herpesvirus 8-driven vascular malignancy classically linked to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-associated immunosuppression. Its epidemiology is changing in the antiretroviral therapy (ART) era, and contemporary regional data are limited. Objective We aimed to describe the demographic, clinical, pathological, investigative, and treatment characteristics of histologically confirmed KS cases in a large regional health board over a 10-year period. Materials and methods This retrospective observational cohort study covered a 10-year period. Patient demographics, HIV status, CD4 count, where applicable, lesion site and morphology, imaging use, multidisciplinary team discussion, and treatment outcomes were reviewed from electronic medical records. Age at diagnosis was assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by Dunn's post hoc test with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Mortality was compared between HIV-positive and HIV-negative individuals using Fisher's exact test. Results Twenty-six patients were identified; 23 (88%) were male, with a mean age of 52.1 years (range: 31-71 years). Nine patients (35%) were HIV positive, including five patients (19%) newly diagnosed with HIV at KS presentation; 17 (65%) were HIV negative. Fourteen patients (54%) reported having sex with men (MSM). Confirm the numerical data first, and HIV-negative MSM accounted for 23% of the cohort. Four patients (15%) had iatrogenic immunosuppression. T

title: Persistent Anterograde Amnesia Following Multifocal Strategic Ischemic Stroke: A Case Report.
abstract: Strategic ischemic strokes involving memory-related neural circuits can present with prominent cognitive deficits despite relatively limited focal neurological findings. We report a patient who developed persistent anterograde amnesia following an ischemic stroke involving the bilateral thalami, fornix, and pons. Cognitive assessment showed marked impairment in delayed recall, with relative preservation of other domains. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute ischemic lesions in regions critical to memory processing. This case highlights the importance of recognizing strategic infarctions as a potential cause of disproportionate memory impairment and illustrates the relationship between lesion location and the clinical expression of post-stroke amnesia.
summary_short: We report a patient who developed persistent anterograde amnesia following an ischemic stroke involving the bilateral thalami, fornix, and pons.

title: Comparative effects of metformin, semaglutide and tirzepatide on oxidative stress, thiol-disulfide homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage in type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Background and purpose Oxidative stress, impaired thiol-disulfide (DIS) homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage contribute to vascular complications in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We compared redox-related biomarker changes among patients receiving metformin, semaglutide, or tirzepatide and examined associations between thiol-DIS homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage. Experimental approach 141 participants with T2DM were categorised according to prescribed glucose-lowering management and followed for 3 months. Anthropometric measures, glycaemic indices, oxidative stress markers, thiol-DIS homeostasis parameters and serum 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Correlation analyses examined associations with changes in 8-OHdG, and multivariable regression assessed the independent association between changes in native thiol (NT) and 8-OHdG. Key results Improvements in weight, glycaemic control and insulin resistance were observed in all active treatment groups. Greater improvements in redox status and thiol-DIS homeostasis were observed in the semaglutide and tirzepatide groups than in the metformin group. Oxidative DNA damage decreased during follow-up in all active treatment groups, with the greatest reductions observed in the semaglutide and tirzepatide groups. title: Adjunctive ursodeoxycholic acid in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled open-label pilot study.
abstract: Purpose Adequate glycemic control remains difficult to achieve. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) has shown potential glycemic benefits in chronic liver disease patients and anti-inflammatory effects in animal models of type 2 diabetes. This pilot study investigated the effect of UDCA as adjunctive therapy on metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers in patients with type 2 diabetes. Secondary outcomes included fasting blood glucose (FBG), lipid profile, body mass index (BMI), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), high mobility group box 1 (HMGB-1), asprosin, malondialdehyde (MDA), and A-kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1). title: From Nutrients to Acceptance: A Food Science Evaluation of Edible Insects for Sustainable Food Innovation.
abstract: The rapid growth of the global population demands substantial increases in food production. Edible insects, recognized for their minimal land use and superior nutritional profiles, offer a sustainable alternative to traditional livestock. This review examines the potential of four commonly consumed insects, crickets, grasshoppers, mealworms, and black soldier flies, as alternative food sources. This structured narrative review was conducted using a literature search performed in February 2026 in PubMed and Scopus. The search covered publications published between January 2000 and December 2025. Peer-reviewed scientific articles focusing on edible insects for human consumption and addressing nutritional composition, processing, food safety, technological properties, sensory characteristics, consumer acceptance, or sustainable food applications were considered. A total of 1121 records were identified, of which 391 duplicates were removed. After screening and full-text assessment, 44 studies were included in the narrative synthesis. The findings reveal that edible insects, including crickets, grasshoppers, mealworms, and black soldier flies, contain high levels of protein (approximately 35%-70% dry weight), beneficial lipids, vitamins, and essential minerals, whereas exhibiting a lower environmental footprint compared to conventional livestock. title: The bile acid-microbiome-immunity axis in dogs: bile salt hydrolases at the interface of microbial metabolism and intestinal homeostasis.
abstract: Dogs have bile acid pools and gut microbiota that differ from those of humans and rodents, on which most models of bile acids, the microbiome, and immune signaling are based. This review summarizes canine evidence and uses comparative data where canine mechanisms remain unresolved. Microbial bile salt hydrolases deconjugate the taurine-conjugated canine bile acid pool, enabling transformations that impact microbial fitness, intestinal physiology, and FXR and TGR5 signaling. Acute diarrhea and chronic enteropathy are associated with reduced Peptacetobacter hiranonis and baiCD abundance, increased primary bile acids, and decreased secondary fecal bile acids. However, fecal profiles may not represent other intestinal or systemic compartments. Diet also modifies microbial communities and bile acid metabolism. We distinguish direct canine evidence from cross-species inference and identify priorities for spatial and causal studies. Finally, we examine biomarker and therapeutic opportunities, highlighting Lactobacillus johnsonii CNCM I-4884 in canine giardiasis as a focused translational example without implying broad efficacy.
summary_short: Acute diarrhea and chronic enteropathy are associated with reduced Peptacetobacter hiranonis and baiCD abundance, increased primary bile acids, and decreased secondary fecal bile acids.

title: Sarcopenia Assessment in Patients Post Metabolic Surgery With Suboptimal Weight Loss and Outcomes of Subsequent Liraglutide 3.0 mg.
abstract: Sarcopenia risk in post-metabolic surgery populations and in patients subsequently treated with Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) RA raises clinical concern due to potential long-term risks of muscle atrophy, frailty and disability. The aims of secondary data analysis from the BARI-OPTIMISE trial were to determine prevalence of baseline sarcopenia risk and examine the effects of 24 weeks of liraglutide 3.0 mg versus placebo in patients with suboptimal weight loss (WL) post primary metabolic/bariatric surgery (MBS) (sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass) with a poor GLP-1 response. Forty-three patients (46.4 ± 9.8 years, BMI: 42.9 ± 7.37 kg/m2) ≥ 12 months post-MBS with suboptimal WL were given liraglutide 3.0 mg (n = 22), or placebo (n = 21) adjunct to lifestyle intervention (500-kcal daily deficit) for 24 weeks. DEXA measures for appendicular lean mass (ALM), arm lean mass (ARMLM) and body fat mass (BFM) and hand grip strength (HGS) were assessed at baseline and 24 weeks. Different sarcopenia risk methodologies/criteria were applied (EWGSOP2, FNIH and SDOC). Physical functioning tests (HGS, five-times sit-to-stand test [STS], STS power and 6 Minute Walk Test [6MWT]) were measured at baseline and 24 weeks. At baseline, using EWGSOP2 criteria for ALM, ALM index (ALMI) and HGS, 0%-36.4% of patients were at sarcopenia risk. title: Reduction in T-Cell Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity After Reaching a Weight Loss Plateau.
abstract: Experiencing an involuntary weight loss plateau is common after behavioral weight loss. During such periods, sustained negative energy balance activates counterregulatory mechanisms that restore energy balance and may slow further weight loss. However, the cellular bioenergetic changes occurring specifically during a spontaneous weight loss plateau have not been investigated. We studied mitochondrial respiratory capacity in peripheral mononuclear cell populations from participants with obesity, both before and after an intensive lifestyle intervention (ILI). Body weight was tracked continuously over 18 months using a remote electronic scale, enabling retrospective categorization of outcome measures by weight loss phases: active weight loss (aWL), plateau (PL), or regain (RG). Differences in mitochondrial respiration were observed in T cells but not in monocytes across these phases. During aWL, mitochondrial respiratory capacity was similar to pre-ILI; however, basal, ATP-linked, maximal, and spare respiratory capacity were significantly lower during the PL and RG phases. In addition, ATP-linked respiration was lower in the PL and RG, despite higher mitochondrial citrate synthase activity in the PL relative to pre-ILI. These results indicate that T-cell bioenergetics may be responsive to shifts in energy balance during weight reduction. The novel phase-specific classification used in this study uncovers dynamic bioenergetic adaptations that may contribute to a weight loss plat

title: β-Cell Function and Diabetes Outcomes 1 Year After Stopping Oral Baricitinib Immunotherapy for Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: Objective The Baricitinib in New-Onset Type 1 Diabetes (BANDIT) trial showed that baricitinib treatment for 48 weeks preserved β-cell function and lowered insulin requirements and glucose in recent-onset type 1 diabetes. We aimed to determine the durability of these effects following treatment cessation. Research design and methods The following posttreatment outcomes of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled BANDIT trial were analyzed: C-peptide and glucagon responses to a mixed meal, HbA1c, continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) measures, CD8+ T-cell phenotype and function, and adverse events. Results Of 91 randomized participants, 88 (58 baricitinib and 30 placebo) completed the week 96 follow-up. Mean ± SEM C-peptide was significantly greater in baricitinib-treated participants at week 72 (0.54 ± 0.05 vs. 0.38 ± 0.06 pmol/mL; P = 0.015) but not at week 96 (0.43 ± 0.05 vs. 0.35 ± 0.06 nmol/L; P = 0.336). No significant between-group differences in insulin dose, HbA1c, or CGM measures were observed during follow-up. Post hoc comparisons showed that when the study drug was ceased at week 48, baricitinib-treated adults (n = 28) experienced full preservation of β-cell function, whereas C-peptide decreased relative to baseline by 0.09 pmol/mL in baricitinib-treated children (n = 32; P = 0.022). summary_short: Objective The Baricitinib in New-Onset Type 1 Diabetes (BANDIT) trial showed that baricitinib treatment for 48 weeks preserved β-cell function and lowered insulin requirements and glucose in recent-onset type 1 diabetes. We aimed to determine the durability of these effects following treatment cessation.

title: Gallbladder Gangrene Following Bevacizumab Therapy in Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia With Severe Hepatic Involvement and Functional Reclassification of a Synonymous ACVRL1 Variant.
abstract: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia type 2 (HHT2), caused by pathogenic variants in ACVRL1, frequently involves hepatic vascular malformations that may lead to high-output cardiac failure and ischemic biliary complications. Synonymous variants are often classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) without transcript-level validation. We report an integrative clinical and molecular investigation of a patient with severe hepatic involvement and a synonymous ACVRL1 variant. Clinical, imaging, and longitudinal laboratory data were collected. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome sequencing. Functional validation included a minigene splicing assay, RT-PCR analysis of patient-derived skin RNA, and quantitative PCR to assess ACVRL1 transcript expression. A heterozygous ACVRL1 c.474A>T synonymous variant was identified. Functional studies demonstrated activation of a cryptic splice donor site in exon 4, resulting in aberrant transcripts and approximately 50% reduction in ACVRL1 mRNA levels, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay. Clinically, the patient developed gallbladder gangrene following bevacizumab therapy in the setting of diffuse hepatic arteriovenous malformations. Subsequent sirolimus therapy was associated with stabilization of hemoglobin levels and hepatic parameters. summary_short: We report an integrative clinical and molecular investigation of a patient with severe hepatic involvement and a synonymous ACVRL1 variant. Subsequent sirolimus therapy was associated with stabilization of hemoglobin levels and hepatic parameters.

title: The Cardioprotective Effect of Fosinopril on Myocardial Infarction (MI) is Associated With the AMPK/mTOR Pathway.
abstract: To investigate the impact of fosinopril on cardiac function and its regulatory role in autophagy and the AMPK/mTOR pathway in a rat model of myocardial infarction (MI). MI was induced in rats by ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. MI modeling was verified by serum cardiac enzyme assays. Cardiac functions and histological change were determined by echocardiography, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, and Masson's trichrome staining. Autophagy-associated factors were evaluated using western blotting and RT-qPCR. Apoptosis was analyzed by TUNEL assay, while alterations in the phosphorylation of the AMPK/mTOR pathway were determined by western blotting. Serum CK-MB and cTn-I levels were significantly elevated in MI rats, confirming myocardial injury. MI rats showed disordered myocardial architecture with inflammatory infiltration, compromised cardiac function (increased left ventricular end-systolic diameter and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, decreased left ventricular fractional shortening and left ventricular ejection fraction) and myocardial fibrosis. Molecularly, RT-qPCR showed no significant changes in LC3 and p62/SQSTM1 mRNA levels, but Beclin-1 mRNA expression was elevated in MI rats and partially reversed by fosinopril. title: Insights Into Abdominal Wall Vascularized Composite Allotransplantation: An Individual Patient Data Analysis.
abstract: Background Abdominal wall vascularized composite allotransplantation (AWT) has emerged as a reconstructive option for patients with complex abdominal wall defects, particularly in conjunction with intestinal transplantation. Despite more than 2 decades of clinical experience, the available evidence remains limited to isolated case reports and small case series, and important questions regarding patient selection, operative techniques, immunosuppressive strategies, rejection patterns, and clinical outcomes remain unanswered. Therefore, we performed an individual patient data analysis to comprehensively evaluate the current evidence and provide insights into the clinical applicability, efficacy, and limitations of AWT. Methods We conducted a systematic review with an individual patient data analysis in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase were searched through December 2025. Results Twenty studies published between 2003 and 2023 reported 35 individual patients who underwent 37 AWT procedures. The median patient age was 37.5 years (IQR, 17.9), and follow-up ranged from 1 to 7 years. Alemtuzumab was used for induction in 32 patients (91.4%). The principal indications were large abdominal wall defects in 17 patients (48.6%), malignancy in 11 (31.4%), motility disorders in three (8.6%), and vascular disorders and congenital defects in two patients each (5.7%). title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Across Renal Compartments in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) remains a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure despite considerable therapeutic progress. Mitochondrial dysfunction has emerged as a central mechanism linking diabetic metabolic stress to progressive renal injury, yet it is often described as a generalized, whole-kidney abnormality. This view is incomplete because renal compartments differ in metabolic demand, substrate preference, oxygen exposure, mitochondrial density, and repair capacity. Therefore, diabetes is unlikely to induce a uniform mitochondrial defect across the kidney. Here, we introduce a compartment- and stage-specific framework that integrates evidence from proximal tubules, distal nephron segments, glomerular endothelial cells, podocytes, mesangial cells, immune cells, and interstitial compartments. Using this framework, we define how mitochondrial metabolism, dynamics, quality control, redox signaling, mtDNA stress, and inflammatory pathways contribute to DKD progression across distinct renal cell types. We highlight which mitochondrial programs are most clearly implicated in specific renal compartments, where evidence remains limited, and how understudied cell types may contribute to disease progression. This cell- and stage-specific framework provides a basis for interpreting mitochondrial dysfunction by renal compartment and biological context rather than as a single kidney-wide process. title: Schwann Cell-Specific ATG7-Dependent Autophagy Protects Myelin in a Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease.
abstract: Krabbe disease (KD) is a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by severe peripheral demyelination caused by mutations in galactosylceramidase (GALC), leading to the accumulation of galactosylceramide and psychosine. Although psychosine toxicity is central to KD pathology, additional mechanisms likely contribute to myelin dysfunction. Because Schwann cells (SCs) play a critical role in myelin maintenance, and GALC deficiency disrupts lysosomal function, we hypothesized that autophagy is altered in SCs during KD progression. Using a SC-specific Galc conditional knockout (Galc SC cKO) mouse model, we identified early changes in autophagy-related protein levels and increased autophagosome abundance during the pre-symptomatic phase, prior to detectable myelin abnormalities. To assess whether autophagy contributes to disease progression, we selectively deleted Atg7, an essential regulator of canonical autophagy, in SCs. Atg7 deletion alone did not affect myelin or behavior, but its loss in Galc SC cKO mice markedly worsened disease severity. Atg7-Galc SC cKO mice exhibited significantly thinner myelin and pronounced deficits in motor performance and nerve conduction, accompanied by altered steady-state levels of autophagy-associated proteins and functional decline. title: Microgels Containing Protease-Resistant CXCL12 and FasL Enable Long-term Allo-Islet Function Without Systemic Immunosuppression.
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a chronic disease characterized by the autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing β-cells in the pancreas. Replacement of β-cells by islet transplantation has proven to be successful in providing a functional cure for T1D. We previously showed that microencapsulation of allogeneic islets (allo-islets) or xenogeneic islets with CXCL12 promotes β-cell function, provides immune protection, and facilitates vascularization at the graft site in both small- and large-animal models of T1D. In addition, streptavidin-Fas ligand (SA-FasL) microgels induce immune acceptance of allo-islets through expansion of T regulatory cells (Tregs) in combination with short-term systemic immune suppression. This study evaluated a combination of these two complementary approaches for extending allo-islet graft survival in a mouse model of T1D through the codelivery of SA-CXCL12 or a protease-resistant variant of the chemokine (SA-prCXCL12) and SA-FasL within biotinylated microgels in an allogeneic-transplant setting. We demonstrated that microgels coated with SA-FasL and SA-prCXCL12, when cotransplanted with allo-islets, sustained long-term (6 months) diabetes reversal in streptozotocin-treated mice without any systemic immunosuppression more effectively than either agent alone. title: Support to Address Excess Weight and Related Physical Health Conditions for Young People With Severe Mental Illness: A Systematic Review With Narrative and Thematic Synthesis.
abstract: Background Young people with severe mental illness (SMI: psychosis, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder) are at increased risk of experiencing excess weight and related health conditions, such as cardiovascular disease and Type 2 diabetes. Modifiable behavioural factors and antipsychotic-induced weight gain contribute to this risk. Earlier intervention to prevent and mitigate weight gain provides potential opportunity to improve long-term mental and physical health outcomes in this population. Aim To review support provided for young people with SMI, to address excess weight and related physical health conditions. Methods Three electronic databases were searched from January 2010 up to December 2025. Grey literature sources, and references and citations of included material were also searched. Full papers presenting qualitative or quantitative data on young people aged 12-18 years with SMI from high/very high development index countries were eligible for inclusion. Risk of bias for included studies was assessed using a validated tool for each study design. Data were synthesised through narrative and thematic synthesis. Results Seventeen articles describing 15 unique studies met inclusion criteria. title: Investigating the Effect of Gallic Acid During Acute and Chronic Exposure to Acetaldehyde in Liver Cells: Targeting Epigenetic Modifications.
abstract: Acetaldehyde (AcH), a toxic byproduct of ethanol metabolism, causes severe liver damage by binding to proteins and DNA and disrupting their functions. Despite extensive research, effective therapies for AcH-induced toxicity remain limited. This study investigated the protective role of gallic acid (GA), a natural polyphenol, against AcH-induced epigenetic and cellular alterations in WRL 68 cells following acute (24 h) and chronic (14 days) exposure. During acute exposure to AcH, the ability of GA to protect cells from AcH-induced cytotoxicity, DNA damage, and apoptosis was assessed using the MTT assay, DNA fragmentation, AO/EtBr dual staining assays, antioxidant analyses, and expression profiling of miRNAs and histone-modifying enzymes. title: Blood-Derived DNA Methylation Biomarkers Predict Diabetic Kidney Disease and Map to Epigenomic Remodeling in Renal Cells.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease in type 1 diabetes (T1D); however, albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) lack the precision necessary for early prognostication. We sought blood-derived DNA methylation biomarkers that predict DKD progression and reflect renal epigenomic remodeling. In the PROFIL cohort, we performed high-depth genome-wide methylation sequencing of leukocyte DNA from 101 adults with T1D and 20 control participants without diabetes, stratified by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk and observed for a median of 5.6 years. Differentially methylated regions were identified across baseline KDIGO strata and prioritized based on hypomethylation, four or more CpGs per region, and discrimination between KDIGO categories; their associations with eGFR decline and rising albumin excretion were then evaluated. From these candidates, we derived a four-locus methylation risk score (MRS; SLC4A4, FSTL4, ICA1, and PTK2), validated by targeted assays in an independent subset of 330 participants with T1D with low or moderate KDIGO risk at baseline. Those with T1D showed global loss of 5-methylcytosine, with hypomethylated regions enriched at regulatory sites. title: Young ovarian tissue transplantation supports immune homeostasis in post-reproductive female mice through fertility-independent mechanisms
abstract: Reproductive aging is increasingly recognized as a driver of systemic decline in females, yet the ovarian mechanisms linking reproductive senescence to impaired health remain poorly defined. This study tested whether young ovarian tissue exposure supports peripheral immune homeostasis in post-reproductive female mice through fertility-independent mechanisms. Post-reproductive female CBA/J mice received young follicle-containing ovarian tissue transplants or remained as age-matched controls. Circulating immune mediators were analyzed using five multiplex cytokine panels comprising 200 analytes before and after treatment. Peripheral T-cell subsets and naive:memory ratios were assessed by flow cytometry, and thymic histopathology was evaluated at endpoint. Pre-treatment circulating immune profiles were indistinguishable between groups. At 577 days, transplant recipients showed higher AR, CD27L, EGF, IL-17E, IL-1ra, and B7-1/CD80 and lower P-selectin compared with controls. These changes were accompanied by an increase in peripheral memory CD4 + T cells (20.1 ± 4.2% vs. 15.0 ± 1.5%) and a nominal 64% higher CD4 + central naive:memory ratio, consistent with partial preservation of immune competence after reproductive senescence. title: Male chickadees with better spatial cognition sire more extra-pair young
abstract: Across animal taxa, females commonly mate with more than one male, even in monogamous mating systems. These extra-pair copulations and resulting young may increase the fitness of the female via a variety of mechanisms. The ‘good genes’ hypothesis suggests that socially monogamous females mate outside their pair bond to increase the fitness of their offspring via indirect genetic benefits, because extra-pair males do not provide parental care. We tested this hypothesis by quantifying extra-pair paternity in nonmigratory, food-caching mountain chickadees ( Poecile gambeli ). Chickadees rely on spatial cognition to recover scattered food caches, and variation in spatial cognition is associated with increased survival, longer lifespan, and is heritable. However, less is known about the role of sexual selection on spatial cognitive abilities. In the current study, we found that (1) males with better spatial cognitive abilities sired more extra-pair young and produced heavier offspring in their own nests compared to their poorer-performing counterparts, and (2) extra-pair males had significantly better spatial cognition than the social males they cuckolded. These results suggest that sexual selection shapes the evolution of spatial cognition in food-caching chickadees and are consistent with the good genes hypothesis, which posits that females gain indirect genetic benefits via extra-pair young.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and pulmonary outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Pulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet preventive strategies remain limited. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects, but their association with respiratory outcomes in RA is unknown. Using electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of adults with RA and type 2 diabetes mellitus who initiated GLP-1-based therapy or a DPP-4 inhibitor between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2025. Primary coded outcomes were incident coded diagnoses of interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary hypertension (PH) over 3 years, with secondary outcomes including coded bronchiectasis, hospitalization, respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. After matching, 1,656 patients were included in each cohort. Incident ILD occurred in 42 GLP-1RA users versus 54 DPP-4i users with no significant difference (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.57-1.29, p = 0.46). GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced pulmonary hypertension (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.33-0.68, p < 0.001), mechanical ventilation (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35-0.89, p = 0.013), respiratory failure (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.96, p = 0.023), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.00, p = 0.047). title: A review of plant DNA ligases: evolution, molecular functions and applications in crop genetic improvement.
abstract: Genomic DNA constantly suffers endogenous and exogenous genotoxic damage throughout plant growth. DNA ligases catalyze nick sealing and serve core guardians of genome integrity. Plants harbor three major DNA ligase groups addressed in this review: the conserved LIG1 and LIG4 groups and the plant-specific LIG6 group. LIG1 is an essential housekeeping enzyme with dual nuclear-mitochondrial localization, participating in DNA replication, base excision repair and epigenetic demethylation. LIG4 dominates canonical non-homologous end joining for double-strand break repair and competitively balances homologous recombination. Unique LIG6 bears special structural domains and acts as a vital regulator of seed longevity and stress resistance. Despite functional descriptions, the spatiotemporal coordination mechanisms among these three ligases remain unclear. This review systematically summarizes the catalytic mechanisms, evolutionary divergence, subcellular distribution and multifunctional roles of plant DNA ligases, and discusses their application prospects in genome editing and crop seed improvement. Critical unresolved questions including LIG6 biochemical characterization and functional validation across diverse plant species are highlighted, and future research priorities are proposed to advance basic genome stability research and precision breeding utilization.
summary_short: Genomic DNA constantly suffers endogenous and exogenous genotoxic damage throughout plant growth. DNA ligases catalyze nick sealing and serve core guardians of genome integrity.

title: The Aging Surgeon: An American Society of Geriatric Otolaryngology Position Statement on Lifelong Competency and Career Transition.
abstract: BackgroundThe surgical workforce is aging, and projected workforce shortages may drive increasing demand for otolaryngologists to remain in practice later in their careers. Although aging brings heterogeneous cognitive, physical, and sensory changes, age alone is an inadequate predictor of professional competence. Available evidence favors individualized, longitudinal assessment of professional function rather than restriction based on age alone. ASGO identified principles emphasizing career-span assessment, transitions, institutional support, and physician dignity alongside patient safety. Important gaps remain, notably no validated specialty-specific assessment tools.ConclusionsAs more otolaryngologists practice later in their careers, specialty-specific, evidence-informed guidance is needed. Although aging brings heterogeneous cognitive, physical, and sensory changes, age alone is an inadequate predictor of professional competence.

title: Social predictability increases with age in dolphins: A marker of longevity?
abstract: Social ageing research has focused on changes in average social behaviour, overlooking behavioural consistency as a trait. A new PLOS Biology study shows that wild dolphins' grouping patterns become more predictable with age, most markedly in the longest-lived animals.
summary_short: Social ageing research has focused on changes in average social behaviour, overlooking behavioural consistency as a trait. A new PLOS Biology study shows that wild dolphins' grouping patterns become more predictable with age, most markedly in the longest-lived animals.

title: Association analysis of KIAA0825 and SESN3 gene polymorphisms with liver performance in Landes geese.
abstract: 1. Molecular genetic markers offer a means to improve selection efficiency in Landes geese. The objective of this study was to screen for key candidate genes and variant loci involved in the regulation of fatty liver traits in Landes geese.2. A total of 200 geese (100 males and 100 females) were subjected to an overfeeding program. Blood samples from 10 high (HWT) and 10 low liver weight (LWT) female geese were used for whole‑genome resequencing. Differential single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were identified and annotated. Validation was performed in male geese.3. Both the liver weight and liver‑to‑body-weight ratio were significantly higher in the HWT than in the LWT treatment for both sexes. Enriched pathways associated with fatty liver traits included regulation of lipolysis in adipocytes, longevity regulating pathway, axon guidance and glycerolipid metabolism.4. An SNP (T/C) was identified at the chrZ:1905252 locus of the KIAA0825 gene. In female geese, two alleles (T and C) were observed at this Z‑linked locus. The SNP of KIAA0825 was significantly associated with fatty liver weight and individuals carrying the C allele had significantly higher liver weight than those carrying the T allele (p < 0.05). No significant association was found in male geese.5. An SNP (G/A) was identified at chr1:200542695 of the sestrin 3 (SESN3) gene, with three genotypes (GG, GA, AA) present in the population. title: Recurrent but not single falls are associated with frailty in community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and older in Chile.
abstract: Frailty encompasses multiple intrinsic fall risk factors, yet evidence from Latin America remains scarce. Most studies dichotomize frailty and falls, limiting understanding of how frailty phenotypes relate to single or recurrent falls. This study aims to determine the prevalence of single and recurrent falls and their association with frailty in Chilean community-dwelling adults. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted in 2,012 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 60 years from the Alexandros cohort in Santiago, Chile. Falls in the past 12 months were self-reported (0, 1, or ≥ 2). Frailty was assessed considering the Fried phenotype adapted for Chile. Ordinal and binary logistic regression models estimated associations, adjusting for age, sex, BMI category, multimorbidity, and educational attainment. Robustness check and sex-stratified analyses were performed. Participants were 22.9% non-frail, 63.7% pre-frail, and 13.4% frail. Women had higher prevalence of frailty (16.0% vs. 8.3%) and recurrent falls (19.2% vs. 13.4%) than men. Recurrent falls were more frequent in frail participants than in non-frail and pre-frail peers (29.6% vs. 12.0% and 16.6%, p < 0.001). Frailty was associated with higher odds of recurrent falls (adjusted OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.45-2.77), whereas pre-frailty was not (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.93-1.52). Single falls were not significantly associated with frailty or pre-frailty. Findings remained consistent in the robustness check and across sexes. Recurrent, but not si
summary_short: Frailty was associated with higher odds of recurrent falls (adjusted OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.45-2.77), whereas pre-frailty was not (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.93-1.52). Single falls were not significantly associated with frailty or pre-frailty.

title: A Japanese adolescent case of Chung-Jansen syndrome with obesity, diabetes mellitus and a rare missense variant of PHIP p.(Phe17Cys).
abstract: We report on a 13-year-old girl who presented with intellectual disabilities, behavioral abnormalities, dysmorphic features, obesity and diabetes mellitus. Whole-exome sequencing identified a rare PHIP variant (NM_017934.7: c.50T > G p.(Phe17Cys)) in the patient, corresponding to the diagnosis of Chung-Jansen syndrome. At age 16, oral aripiprazole treatment was initiated because behavioral problems and anxiety aggravated. Subsequently, chronic hyperglycemia and obesity worsened. At age 18, hemoglobin A1c and body mass index increased to 9.4% and 33 kg/m2. The initiation of subcutaneous insulin and tirzepatide therapy successfully improved her glycemic control. This is the first report to describe the detailed clinical phenotype of the PHIP p.(Phe17Cys) variant, providing valuable insight into pathogenicity despite its previous registration in ClinVar and gnomAD.
summary_short: At age 18, hemoglobin A1c and body mass index increased to 9.4% and 33 kg/m2. The initiation of subcutaneous insulin and tirzepatide therapy successfully improved her glycemic control.

title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Treatment on Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits with anti-inflammatory and anti-arrhythmic properties. This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLP-1 use with postoperative atrial fibrillation and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from 2010 to 2025. Patients were stratified into GLP-1 users and non-users. Patients with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF), concurrent MAZE procedure, and prior cardioversions or ablations were excluded. The primary outcome was incidence of new onset postoperative AF within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included AF-related readmissions and all-cause mortality. Multivariable adjusted regression models were used to compare POAF incidence and time-to-event secondary outcomes. A total of 8,672 patients were included. The 411 GLP-1 users were younger with higher BMI and HbA1c and were more likely to have diabetes compared to non-users (all p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, GLP-1 users demonstrated a significantly lower incidence of postoperative AF compared to non-users (29.0% vs. 34.6%, RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.99, p=0.038). AF-related readmission in GLP-1 users were 1.2% at 1 year and 3.5% at 5 years, compared to 2.9% and 6.5% in non-users, respectively (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.30-1.13, p=0.111). One- and five-year mortality was similar between groups (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.25, p=0.561). In this la
summary_short: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits with anti-inflammatory and anti-arrhythmic properties. This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLP-1 use with postoperative atrial fibrillation and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

title: Effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes and their association with weight loss: a substudy of the randomised, double-masked, parallel-group, phase 3a REDEFINE 2 trial.
abstract: CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, demonstrated substantial weight loss versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes in REDEFINE 2. We aimed to evaluate glycaemic outcomes in a subgroup of participants who underwent continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). REDEFINE 2 was a global 68-week, double-masked, parallel-group phase 3a trial that included 1206 adults from 12 countries with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes who were randomly assigned (3:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg or placebo. Participants were assigned treatment using a centralised web-based system. Participants, investigators, site staff, and the sponsor were masked to group allocation throughout the trial. A subgroup of 199 participants from 35 US sites (including university hospitals, health-care centres, research centres, and other centres) were equipped with a CGM device (Dexcom G6 Pro) for double-masked measurements from week -3 to 0, week 20 to 24, and week 64 to 68. Prespecified secondary endpoints included change in time in range (TIR; 3·9-10·0 mmol/L) and change in time in tight range (TITR; 3·9-7·8 mmol/L) for CagriSema versus placebo. REDEFINE 2 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05394519, and is completed. Between Feb 1 and Aug 11, 2023, 199 participants were enrolled in the CGM subgroup (149 in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and 50 in the placebo group) and had their CGM data analysed.
summary_short: CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, demonstrated substantial weight loss versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes in REDEFINE 2. We aimed to evaluate glycaemic outcomes in a subgroup of participants who underwent continuous glucose…

title: Impact of preoperative GLP-1 agonist use on patient-reported outcomes in obese patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a propensity score match analysis.
abstract: Obesity has traditionally been associated with increased perioperative risk in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), originally developed for diabetes management, have recently emerged as an effective strategy for weight loss. Although recent literature has suggested that GLP-1 RA use may reduce postoperative complications following TKA, their impact on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) remains unclear. A retrospective review of an institutional database identified 11,025 consecutive patients who underwent primary TKA. After exclusion, a 1:3 propensity score-matched analysis was performed to balance baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, yielding 146 obese patients who used preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonists and 438 matched non-users. Evaluated PROMs included SF-10a, PROMIS Global Mental and Physical, and KOOS-PS. Clinically meaningful improvement was assessed using the Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID). Secondary outcomes included 90-day and one- and two-year complications. There were no significant differences between GLP-1 RA users and non-users in preoperative or postoperative PROM scores, delta scores, or the proportion of patients achieving MCID improvement across SF-10a, PROMIS Global Mental, PROMIS Global Physical, or KOOS-PS (P > 0.05 for all). Rates of 90-day medical complications, including pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, and surgica
summary_short: Obesity has traditionally been associated with increased perioperative risk in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

title: The Intrarenal See-Saw: Differentiating the Hemodynamic and Electrolyte Effects of Glucagon and Glucagon-Like-Peptide-1 Receptor Therapies.
abstract: The management of metabolic disease is undergoing a paradigm shift with the transition from single-agent glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) to novel dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonists. While GLP-1RAs offer established, weight-independent cardiorenal protection, the intentional therapeutic agonism of glucagon, a hormone historically targeted for suppression, introduces profound and largely unexamined physiological shifts. This review clarifies the distinct, often opposing, mechanisms of these hormones, focusing specifically on their divergent roles in kidney hemodynamics and tubular solute handling. Evolutionarily, glucagon defends against starvation by driving hepatic gluconeogenesis and ureagenesis, but its kidney hemodynamic effects are highly context-dependent. Experimental models suggest glucagon may trigger tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF)-mediated glomerular hyperfiltration via proximal Na+/amino acid co-transport after a protein meal, and via direct thick ascending limb (TAL) stimulation during fasting, though long-term human data remain limited. In contrast, GLP-1 coordinates the fed state, inducing proximal natriuresis via Na+/H+ exchanger 3 (NHE3) inhibition while concurrently acting as a kidney vasodilator, effectively uncoupling distal sodium delivery from tubuloglomerular feedback. title: Incretin-Based Medications for Obesity Management: Their Relationships to Mental Health, Eating Disorders, and Substance Use Disorders.
abstract: This narrative review examines the relationship between incretin-based medications (principally semaglutide and tirzepatide) and mental health, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. In obesity trials, semaglutide and tirzepatide did not worsen depressive symptoms or increase suicidal ideation or behavior, but most evidence comes from participants without major psychiatric illness. The medications consistently improved weight-related psychosocial quality of life, while effects on broader mental health quality of life were less consistent. Early data suggest potential benefit for binge eating disorder, though evidence remains limited. There are also concerns about misuse and possible worsening of restrictive eating in people with eating disorders. Preliminary findings indicate these drugs may reduce alcohol craving and heavy drinking, and there are limited data pertaining to other substance use disorders. Semaglutide and tirzepatide appear to have generally favorable mental health and psychosocial effects. However, more long-term, targeted studies of these and other novel incretin-based medications are needed in people with psychiatric illness, certain eating disorders, and substance use disorders.
summary_short: Early data suggest potential benefit for binge eating disorder, though evidence remains limited. Preliminary findings indicate these drugs may reduce alcohol craving and heavy drinking, and there are limited data pertaining to other substance use disorders.

title: The Metabolic Window of Conception: A Clinical Framework for the GLP-1 Era.
abstract: In brief: GLP-1 receptor agonists can restore ovulation before reproductive safety is established, leaving many users in an unmanaged conception window. We propose a three-phase metabolic window of conception framework with a preconception metabolic optimisation checklist to make that window planned rather than accidental.

title: Comparative analysis of tyrosine kinase pathway inhibition, cell viability and immunohistochemical expression in canine and human urothelial carcinoma cell lines.
abstract: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder is a highly aggressive neoplasm in both humans and dogs, with the canine model representing a valuable tool for comparative oncology. This study aimed to characterize the immunohistochemical labelling of tyrosine kinases receptors (TKRs) and components of the MAPK pathway, as well as to evaluate the in-vitro response to targeted therapies in canine (AXC) and human (T24) urothelial carcinoma cell lines under two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) cell culture. Immunohistochemical analysis of the cell lines revealed greater labelling of VEGFR-2 and PDGFR-β, while EGFR and HER2 showed low or no immunolabelling, particularly in T24 cells. Functional assays demonstrated that lapatinib and sorafenib exerted the most pronounced cytotoxic effects in 2D culture, significantly reducing cell viability in both models. Toceranib also showed relevant activity, whereas rapamycin and palbociclib gave variable responses. Gene expression analysis, assessed by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction, showed that treatment with lapatinib and sorafenib modulated key genes, including EGFR, ERBB-2, c-KIT, MAPK, PDGFR-β and VEGFR-2. Three-D culture models had reduced drug sensitivity, particularly in T24 cells, with increased cell viability after exposure to certain agents, highlighting the influence of tumour architecture on therapeutic response. title: Effect of metformin on HIV reservoir, inflammation and cell differentiation in non-diabetic older people with HIV: a two-year placebo-controlled pilot trial (Metforaging).
abstract: People with HIV (PWH) on long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) exhibit persistent inflammation, immune activation, and a stable HIV reservoir, contributing to non-AIDS age-related comorbidities. Metformin, an indirect mTOR inhibitor with immunometabolic properties, is a candidate geroprotective agent. We assessed its long-term immunological and virological impact in non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥50 years. Metforaging is a phase II, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in which 35 non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥ 50 years received metformin or placebo for 96 weeks. At baseline and week 96, we quantified blood T-cell, monocyte, B-cell and NK subsets, inflammation and immune checkpoint biomarkers, total HIV DNA, intact/defective proviruses, and cell-associated HIV RNA (CA-RNA). Between-group effects were estimated by baseline-adjusted ANCOVA. At week 96, CD8+ TEMRA T cells increased with placebo but remained stable under metformin (adjusted mean difference -5.2%, 95% CI -8.5 to -2.0; p=0.003), with a modest increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (p=0.044). No between-group differences were detected in soluble inflammation or immune checkpoint biomarkers, immune checkpoint mRNA expression, or HIV reservoir markers (total HIV DNA, intact and defective proviruses, CA-RNA). title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is not associated with risk of incident inflammatory bowel disease in U.S. adults.
abstract: Some observational studies have linked higher dietary sugar intake to increased risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), though few studies have evaluated diabetes and IBD risk. Here, we examined the relationship between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and incident IBD. We utilized data comprising 225 328 U.S. adults (mean baseline age 46 years) from the prospective Nurses' Health Study (1986-2020), Nurses' Health Study II (1991-2021), and Health Professionals Follow-Up Study (1986-2020). We excluded those with IBD at baseline and type 1 diabetes mellitus. We confirmed T2DM via validated questionnaires and IBD through medical record review. Using Cox proportional hazards models, we estimated hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) according to diagnosis of T2DM, adjusting for confounders. We also examined hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and metformin use and IBD risk. We documented 391 CD and 510 UC cases over 6 171 602 person-years of follow-up. T2DM was not associated with risk of CD (P = .28) or UC (P = .79). Compared with participants without T2DM, those with T2DM had an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.44-1.27) for CD and 1.06 (95% CI, 0.69-1.62) for UC. In participants with available HbA1c (n = 5900), there was no association between having at least prediabetes (HbA1c ≥5.7) and risk IBD (all P ≥ .32). Metformin use was also not associated with IBD risk (all P ≥ .15). T2DM was not associated with incident CD o

title: Exercise to Enhance Mitophagy in Parkinson's Disease - A Narrative Review.
abstract: Mitophagy is a central mechanism in mitochondrial quality control and essential for neuronal health. It is impaired in Parkinson's disease (PD) and mutations of a number of genes associated with mitophagy cause familial PD. Recent advances in the development of novel treatment strategies for PD include phase I clinical trials for selective mitophagy enhancers. Next to pharmacological approaches, specific lifestyles, such as regular physical exercise, can promote mitophagy and thereby mitochondrial health and may be safer than pharmacological approaches and associated with many other health benefits. Here we explore, whether the well-known benefits of exercise for PD brain may be mediated by improved mitophagy. We put the potential benefits of mitophagy in the context of other exercise-induced, brain-health promoting mechanisms with relevance for PD and summarize the available literature investigating the role of mitophagy in therapeutic effects of exercise in models of PD. While the potential of exercise to promote mitophagy and brain health is well established, little direct evidence exists that implicates mitophagy as mediator of beneficial effects of exercise on PD symptoms and progression. Based on the identified knowledge gaps, we reflect on how this interaction may be studied in the future.

title: Co-metabolic removal of perfluorooctanoic acid and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid by marine diatom Chaetoceros calcitrans MZB-1 using positively-charged organic compounds and common carbon sources.
abstract: While microalgae can degrade emerging pollutants, the removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) remains limited, which can be effectively improved via co-metabolism. The impacts of six common carbon sources and three positively-charged organic compounds on the removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) by marine diatom Chaetoceros calcitrans MZB-1 were studied, focusing on the potential biological mechanism underlying the co-metabolism. Among the common carbon sources, sodium succinate (200 mg/L) was suitable for enhancing removal of PFOA, while glycine (500 mg/L) was beneficial for the better removal of PFOS, with removal efficiencies increasing to 38.16% and 37.56%, respectively. This stimulation was accompanied by an induction of key degrading enzymes, i.e. cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) for PFOA and taurine dioxygenase (TauD) for PFOS in microalgae. Among the three positively-charged organic compounds, lysine (Lys, 100 mg/L) and arginine (Arg, 200 mg/L) were beneficial for the elimination of PFOA and PFOS, respectively, with corresponding removal efficiencies of 39.24% and 42.78%. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and zeta potential measurement indicated that the binding of NH3+ group in Arg and Lys to the COO- group on the algal surface led to a decrease in surface negative charge, thereby enhancing the biosorption of PFOA and PFOS. Meanwhile, amino acids accelerated the growth of the alga and the se
summary_short: While microalgae can degrade emerging pollutants, the removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) remains limited, which can be effectively improved via co-metabolism.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Versus Metformin for Adults on Antipsychotics.
abstract: Objective Evidence for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1s) to treat antipsychotic-associated weight gain is limited. A comparison of 52-week weight loss with semaglutide/tirzepatide versus metformin in adults taking antipsychotics was conducted using nationwide electronic health record data. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Truveta database. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to compare the percent initial weight loss between GLP-1 and metformin users. Weight loss by diabetes status, antipsychotic type, medication adherence, and type of GLP-1 medication (semaglutide vs. tirzepatide) was evaluated. Results The cohort included 10,424 adults initiating semaglutide or tirzepatide and 22,788 initiating metformin while taking antipsychotics. Mean weight change was -7.5% ± 0.1% with GLP-1s versus -1.7% ± 0.1% with metformin ( p p Conclusions Semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with substantially greater weight loss than metformin in adults taking antipsychotics. Improving medication continuity may enhance treatment effectiveness in this population.

title: Autophagy Markers in Primary Hyperparathyroidism.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate serum Beclin-1, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) levels, and their associations with primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT)-related biochemical changes and complications in patients with PHPT. Methods Forty-two individuals with PHPT and 42 healthy individuals without any systemic disease were included in the study. Serum Beclin-1 and mTOR levels were measured by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay method. Results Compared to controls, the PHPT group exhibited significantly lower serum Beclin-1 and higher mTOR levels. There was no significant difference in Beclin-1 and mTOR levels in PHPT cases with or without osteoporosis (OP) or urolithiasis. mTOR levels were positively correlated with parathyroid hormone (PTH), serum corrected calcium (cCa) and adenoma volume, and negatively correlated with 25OHD vitamin. Serum Beclin-1 level was positively correlated with phosphorus level and negatively correlated with PTH, cCa, and adenoma volume. Conclusion The altered profiles of mTOR and Beclin-1 in PHPT suggest an association between the disease state and suppressed systemic autophagic activity. This pattern correlates positively with parathyroid adenoma volume and disease severity markers (PTH and cCa).
summary_short: Conclusion The altered profiles of mTOR and Beclin-1 in PHPT suggest an association between the disease state and suppressed systemic autophagic activity.

title: Skin manifestations and prescribing patterns in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a multinational study.
abstract: Objective To describe the clinical characteristics and treatments of women with PMOS-related skin concerns presenting to specialist clinics internationally and within the United Kingdom (UK). Methods This retrospective observational study included women with suspected or confirmed PMOS attending eight specialist centers across five countries between January 2020 and December 2023. No lower age limit was specified; all participants were aged ≥16 years. Clinical records provided data on dermatological manifestations and treatments, including doses and formulations, before and after specialist consultation. Results Of 1313 participants, 1041 (79.3%) had at least one dermatological manifestation; among these, 90.1% had hirsutism, 36.4% had acne, and 6.6% had specialist dermatological review. Metformin and progesterone-only pill predominated in the first and second medication records overall, respectively; in the UK, these were metformin and spironolactone. Prescribing varied significantly across countries and between UK centers. Hirsutism predominated across age groups. In the first medication record, metformin predominated except at ages 16-24, when the combined oral contraceptive pill predominated. Where documented, the most common doses were metformin 1000 mg/day and spironolactone 100 mg/day. Ethnicity closely aligned with recruitment country, limiting interpretation of ethnic differences. title: Pharmacogenomic Modulators of Drug Transport, Detoxification, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation: Insights from SLC22A2, GSTP1, SOD2 and TNF-α for precision medicine.
abstract: Background: Interindividual variability in drug response remains a fundamental clinical problem, arising from the combined influence of genetic, physiological, and environmental factors. This review examines four pharmacogenomically significant genes, SLC22A2, GSTP1, SOD2 and TNF-α, involved in drug transport, detoxification, oxidative stress and inflammatory pathways. Method: Clinical evidence linking variants of these genes to altered drug responses, toxicity profiles and therapeutic outcomes was evaluated. Results: SLC22A2 (OCT2) influences renal uptake of metformin, cisplatin and aminoglycosides. Its variants modify treatment response, and increase individual susceptibility to nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. GSTP1 is a major Phase II metabolic enzyme. Its variants affect detoxification, oxidative stress and may cause chemotherapy resistance. SOD2 is an antioxidant enzyme that protects mitochondria from damage. Its variants alter ROS handling and increase risk of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and platinum-induced tissue injury. TNF-α variants amplify inflammatory cascades and are associated with variability in autoimmune drug response and immunotherapy-related inflammation. Conclusion: These genes act across interconnected pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic pathways, so studying their polymorphisms together can explain interindividual variability better than single-gene analysis. Combined genotyping of these genes has the potential to improve drug safety, toxicity predicti
summary_short: SOD2 is an antioxidant enzyme that protects mitochondria from damage. TNF-α variants amplify inflammatory cascades and are associated with variability in autoimmune drug response and immunotherapy-related inflammation.

title: Intranasal Coadministration of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Protein and a Live Attenuated Influenza Vector Provides Potent Systemic and Mucosal Protection in Mice.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of severe acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants, and an approved active pediatric vaccine is lacking. Potential challenges in vaccine development include concerns about vaccine-enhanced respiratory disease (VERD) reported with some intramuscular formulations and the limited immunogenicity often observed with live attenuated intranasal vaccines. Here, we present an intranasal RSV vaccine combining the prefusion F (pre-F) protein, a key component of recently approved RSV vaccines, with a live attenuated influenza virus vector (dNS1-RBD) that previously received emergency use authorization in China for COVID-19. This combined strategy synergistically enhanced both systemic and mucosal immune responses in mice, inducing robust serum-neutralizing antibodies and critical mucosal IgA. Heat inactivation reduced the mucosal adjuvant effect of the attenuated influenza vector. Compared with that of intramuscular AS01 E -adjuvanted pre-F, our intranasal vaccine demonstrated superior mucosal immunity and comparable protection against RSV challenge across all doses, effectively clearing lung and nasal turbinate viruses and preventing pathogenicity. This approach offers a promising platform for pediatric RSV vaccination, leveraging attenuated influenza vectors to elicit comprehensive protective immunity.
summary_short: Heat inactivation reduced the mucosal adjuvant effect of the attenuated influenza vector.

title: Short-term repeatability of saliva-based epigenetic age measurements: implications for longitudinal intervention studies.
abstract: Epigenetic age measures are increasingly used as longitudinal outcomes in aging and intervention studies, but interpretation of within-person change requires knowledge of short-term measurement variability. We quantified technical and repeated-collection variability of epiAge, a saliva-based targeted next-generation sequencing DNA methylation age estimate derived from age-related methylation within the ELOVL2 locus. Ninety-four adults provided saliva at up to three time points separated by 48 hours. Samples were anonymized, analyzed in a blinded laboratory, and processed in technical triplicate. Technical variability was low, with a mean SD of 1.04 years across triplicates in 255 saliva samples and an ICC of 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.94) in the 212-sample complete three-visit subset. Across repeated saliva collections, the mean absolute first-to-last difference was 2.22 years, with a mean difference of 0.74 years and 95% limits of agreement from -5.61 to 7.09 years. Among 71 participants completing all three collections, mean within-individual SD was 1.58 years and repeated-collection ICC was 0.85 (95% CI 0.79-0.90). Variance-component analysis attributed 81.3% of variability to between-person differences, 11.5% to between-visit variation, and 7.1% to technical variability. These findings define the short-term variability that should be considered when interpreting epigenetic age change in longitudinal and intervention studies.
summary_short: Epigenetic age measures are increasingly used as longitudinal outcomes in aging and intervention studies, but interpretation of within-person change requires knowledge of short-term measurement variability. We quantified technical and repeated-collection variability of epiAge, a saliva-based targeted next-generation…

title: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults following asymptomatic COVID-19 infection.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been linked to new-onset hyperglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, and diabetes mellitus. Emerging evidence suggests it may also trigger, or unmask, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA). We describe a previously nondiabetic adult who developed symptomatic hyperglycemia 5 to 6 weeks after confirmed COVID-19 infection, presenting with polyuria, polydipsia, and a hemoglobin A1c above 13% (reference range, <5.7%). Despite severe hyperglycemia, the patient had an inappropriately normal C-peptide level of 2.7 ng/mL (SI: 900 pmol/L) (reference range, 1.1-4.4 ng/mL [SI: 360-1460 pmol/L]), and autoimmune testing was positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 and zinc transporter 8 antibodies, indicating autoimmune β-cell dysfunction. The combination of subacute onset, presence of islet autoantibodies, and partially preserved insulin secretion supported a diagnosis of LADA, and insulin therapy was ultimately initiated. This case contributes to growing reports of COVID-19-associated LADA and highlights the importance of recognizing autoimmune diabetes in adults with new-onset hyperglycemia following severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection. Because LADA can present gradually and resemble type 2 diabetes mellitus, misclassification may delay appropriate management.
summary_short: Emerging evidence suggests it may also trigger, or unmask, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA).

title: Successful treatment of symptomatic locally recurrent unresectable pheochromocytoma with percutaneous ablations.
abstract: Metastatic or locally recurrent pheochromocytomas (PCCs) present significant therapeutic challenges, particularly in patients with symptomatic or progressive disease. Current treatment options, apart from surgery, are predominantly palliative. Minimally invasive percutaneous ablative techniques have emerged as promising treatment modalities for selected patients with unresectable or metastatic PCCs. We report a case of a woman with neurofibromatosis type 1 with a symptomatic, progressive unresectable 3.3 cm PCC recurrence in the adrenal bed following 2 prior surgical resections. Three consecutive percutaneous ablations-2 cryoablations followed by irreversible electroporation led to clinical, biochemical, and radiographic resolution of the disease. Preprocedural medical management with terazosin, metyrosine, and atenolol was essential in ensuring the safety of the interventions. The patient demonstrated sustained local and biochemical disease control at 4 years of follow-up. This case illustrates the effectiveness of repeated ablative therapies in achieving sustained remission in unresectable recurrent PCC and emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary care.
summary_short: We report a case of a woman with neurofibromatosis type 1 with a symptomatic, progressive unresectable 3.3 cm PCC recurrence in the adrenal bed following 2 prior surgical resections.

title: Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic use, de-escalation, and outcomes in Enterobacterales bloodstream infections: a retrospective observational study.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate empirical and definitive antibiotic prescribing practices and outcomes of patients with bloodstream infection (BSI) due to Enterobacterales. Methods A retrospective observational study enrolling all consecutive adult patients admitted to the Emergency Department of Niguarda Hospital, Italy, with a monomicrobial BSI due to an Enterobacterales from January 2019 to December 2023 was performed. Results 667 patients with a BSI due Enterobacterales were enrolled, 57.1% with sepsis and 16.5% with septic shock. Third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCR-E) accounted for 25.6% and were associated with a 10-fold higher risk of inappropriate empirical therapy (OR 10.7; 95%confidence interval (CI) 6.10-18.74). Piperacillin-tazobactam was the most frequently prescribed empiric antibiotic in the entire cohort (54.3%). Among patients with non-3GCR-E BSI, 57.7% received unnecessary broad-spectrum empiric coverage with piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenems, yet de-escalation occurred in only 31.7% of those eligible. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 10.2%, with no difference between 3GCR-E and non-3GCR-E BSI (OR 0.89; 95%CI 0.49-1.6). Mortality was associated with age (OR 1.55; 95%CI 1.17-2.06), Charlson Comorbidity Index (OR 1.24; 95%CI 1.12-1.38), immunosuppression (OR 2.07; 95%CI 1.1-3.95), respiratory infection (OR 3.13; 95%CI 1.28-7.65) and septic shock (OR 5.49; 95%CI 2.95-10.21), whereas urinary tract infection was associated with higher su

title: Hematopoietic Stem Cells: Bone Marrow Niche, Origination, Differentiation, Diseases, and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) sustain lifelong hematopoiesis, with developmental programs and the bone marrow niche governing their fate. However, how niche alterations and epigenetic dysregulation jointly contribute to malignant evolution remains incompletely understood. This article reviews HSCs origin and differentiation, with particular emphasis on the roles of endosteal, vascular, and perivascular niches. The regulatory mechanisms underlying stemness are examined through the lens of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation, histone modifications, and three-dimensional (3D) chromatin organization. The mechanisms by which abnormalities in DNA methyltransferase 3 alpha, tet methylcytosine dioxygenase 2, and additional sex combs like 1 promote the progression of clonal hematopoiesis toward myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia are summarized. The review also discusses drug resistance and relapse mediated by leukemia stem cells, along with epigenetic- and niche-targeted therapeutic strategies. The review also evaluates strategies to improve existing DNA methyltransferase, enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), and histone deacetylases inhibitors. The review also explores rational combination approaches involving dual-function degraders, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and epigenetic immunomodulators, as well as emerging strategies based on transplantation, gene editing, and niche targeting. title: Hematopoietic role of naringin phytosome against phenylhydrazine-induced hemolytic anemia in rats.
abstract: Background The World Health Organization reports that around 25% of the worldwide population suffers from anemia, with nearly 50% of these instances seen among preschool-aged children. Naringin has numerous biological functions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, lipid-lowering, cardiovascular-protective, and gut-protective effects. The current study aims to evaluate the potential therapeutic effect of naringin phytosome on phenylhydrazine (PHZ)-induced hemolytic anemia in rats. Hemolytic anemia was induced in male rats by intraperitoneal (i.p.) administration of PHZ (40 mg/kg) for 2 days. The animals are divided into five groups (n = 6): The control group and the hemolytic anemia (HA) groups, which were administered distilled water orally for six subsequent days. The treated groups received naringin (100 mg/kg), free phytosome (45 mg/kg), or naringin phytosome (45 mg/kg) for 6 days. Results Naringin phytosome treatment resulted in considerable improvement in hematological, renal, hepatic, and inflammatory biomarkers. In addition, it decreases malonaldehyde, nitric Oxide, matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP-9), and DNA fragmentation levels, and increases membrane palmitoylated protein 1 (MPP-1) and antioxidant parameters in the liver, kidney, and spleen. title: Induced Dimerization Tools to Deplete Specific Phosphatidylinositol Phosphates.
abstract: Chemical dimerization systems have been used to drive acute depletion of polyphosphoinositides (PPIn). They do so by inducing subcellular localization of enzymes that catabolize the PPIn. By using this approach, all seven PPIn can be depleted in living cells and in real time. The rapid permeation of dimerizer agents and the specific expression of recruiter proteins confer great spatial and temporal resolution with minimal cell perturbation. In this chapter, we provide detailed instructions to monitor and induce depletion of PPIn in live cells.

title: Impact of Concomitant Medication Use on Treatment Outcomes in Patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors.
abstract: Introduction Concomitant medications such as statins, aspirin, and metformin may modulate immune responses and influence outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Their impact in advanced renal cell carcinoma (aRCC) remains unclear. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 400 patients with aRCC treated with ICIs at Winship Cancer Institute of Emory University from 2018 to 2023. Baseline medication use, defined as active prescription at the time of ICI initiation, was documented. Clinical end points included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and disease control rate (DCR). Kaplan-Meier estimates, Cox proportional hazards models, and multivariable regression were used to assess associations between medication use and outcomes. Results At baseline, 42.5% of patients were on statins, 34.5% on aspirin, and 12.3% on metformin. Median follow-up was 43.0 months. Statin use was associated with improved DCR (odds ratio, 1.85; p = 0.008), with a positive trend observed for PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.81; p = 0.071) in univariable analysis. However, no significant independent associations were observed in multivariable models for overall survival (HR, 0.92; p = 0.629), PFS (HR, 0.90; p = 0.410), or DCR (odds ratio, 1.48; p = 0.119). Aspirin and metformin use were not significantly associated with outcomes in univariable analyses and were excluded from multivariable models. title: Motoric cognitive risk syndrome identifies older adults at risk of functional decline in rural South Africa
abstract: Background Functional decline and dementia are rising rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa. Motoric cognitive risk (MCR) syndrome, characterized by slow gait and subjective memory complaints, may offer an accessible marker of vulnerability. This study aimed to estimate MCR prevalence and incidence, examine longitudinal motor–cognitive phenotype changes, and assess associations with functional decline and mortality among older South Africans. We analyzed 2163 adults aged ≥ 60 years from the Health and Aging in Africa Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH community in South Africa (HAALSI) cohort (2014–2022), classified as healthy, memory-only, gait-only, and MCR. We compared phenotypes at baseline and an approximately 7-year follow-up (including suspected dementia). Logistic and Cox regression models evaluated associations with worsening activities of daily living (ADLs), grip strength decline, and mortality, with death included as a separate outcome in a complementary multinomial analysis. Baseline MCR prevalence was 5.4%, with an incidence rate of 9.79 per 1000 person-years (95% CI 7.44–12.66). Transitions were dynamic: 23.9% of MCR participants reverted to the healthy phenotype over 7 years, while 2.6% developed suspected dementia. MCR was associated with worsening ADLs after full adjustment (OR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.21 to 4.12, p = 0.029), whereas memory-only and gait-only phenotypes were not.
