title: Association of sleep patterns with organ aging: a large community-based study
abstract: Sleep plays an essential role in biological processes, but its relationship with biological aging is under-explored. We examined the relationship between sleep patterns and both organ age gaps and accelerated organ aging. This study included 247,697 participants without major chronic disease, from the UK Biobank (mean age: 55.20 ± 8.09). Eight organ system-specific ages (cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain) were constructed using machine learning, incorporating biomarker, physiological, anthropometric, and neuroimaging data. Organ-specific age gaps (the difference between estimated age and chronological age) were calculated, and accelerated organ aging was defined as an organ age gap exceeding the 95th percentile. Sleep patterns were self-reported at baseline, comprising sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness, and were classified into healthy, intermediate, and poor. Having a poor compared to a healthy sleep pattern was related to significantly higher organ-specific age gaps for all but one organ (specifically pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain), and was associated with faster pulmonary (OR 1.251, 95%CI: 1.116–1.404), hepatic (OR 1.382, 95%CI: 1.235–1.546), musculoskeletal (OR 1.708, 95%CI: 1.491–1.957), immune (OR 1.428, 95%CI: 1.292–1.579), metabolic (OR 1.659, 95%CI: 1.477–1.864), and brain (OR 1.592, 95%CI: 1.132–2.240) aging, as well as related to sig

title: Obesity impairs ovarian reserve and follicular dynamics in rodents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Obesity and obesity-related metabolic dysfunction have been proposed to accelerate ovarian aging, yet their stage-specific effects on ovarian reserve remain unclear. We systematically evaluated follicular abundance in rodent models of diet-induced obesity (DIO) and genetic obesity. We searched Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE, and Scopus through May 2026. We synthesized controlled studies reporting quantitative ovarian reserve-related outcomes using multilevel random-effects models with standardized mean differences (SMD; Hedges’ g ). Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, subgroup/meta-regression analyses, sensitivity analyses, and small-study effects were assessed. Fifty-two studies were included, of which 42 contributed to quantitative synthesis. DIO reduced primordial follicle count (24 studies; 34 effect sizes; SMD = − 1.54; 95% CI − 2.56 to − 0.52; p = 0.003), remaining significant after outlier exclusion (SMD = − 1.05; 95% CI − 1.89 to − 0.20; p = 0.015). Secondary follicle count was also reduced (SMD = − 1.05; 95% CI − 1.90 to − 0.21; p = 0.014), whereas follicular atresia increased (SMD = 3.15; 95% CI 2.03 to 4.27; p < 0.001). No associations were detected for DIO and primary or antral follicles or corpus luteum count. Genetic obesity was also associated with lower primordial (SMD = − 2.32; 95% CI − 3.73 to − 0.91; p = 0.001) and primary follicle counts (SMD = − 2.61; 95% CI − 3.87 to − 1.36; p < 0.001). title: Krüppel regulates cell cycle exit and limits adult neurogenesis of mushroom body neural progenitors in Drosophila
abstract: Neural progenitors typically exit the cell cycle during development, limiting adult neurogenesis. Here, we identify Krüppel (Kr) as a regulator of cell cycle exit and elimination of mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) in Drosophila . Neuroblast (NB)-specific Kr RNAi and the Irregular facet ( KrIf-1 ) mutation prolong MBNB lifespan and enable continued adult neurogenesis. Despite low post-embryonic expression, pupal stage-specific Kr depletion or misexpression causes MBNB retention, revealing a role distinct from its established embryonic function. Persistent MBNBs retain the early temporal factor IGF2 mRNA-binding protein (Imp) and fail to fully induce the late temporal factors Syncrip (Syp) and Eip93F (E93). Imp co-depletion suppresses MBNB retention following Kr depletion, identifying Imp as a key downstream effector. Krüppel homolog 1 (Kr-h1), a hormone-responsive transcription factor, functionally antagonises Kr by suppressing E93 expression. Kr-h1 knockdown partially rescues MBNB retention caused by Kr depletion, whereas its overexpression drives tumour-like NB overgrowth. Together, these findings identify Kr as a lineage-specific regulator coordinating the Imp/Syp transition and E93 expression to promote timely MBNB termination. This work reveals how temporal regulators control neural progenitor lifespan and restrict adult neurogenesis, linking intrinsic developmental programmes with hormone-responsive pathways in the Drosophila brain.
summary_short: This work reveals how temporal regulators control neural progenitor lifespan and restrict adult neurogenesis, linking intrinsic developmental programmes with hormone-responsive pathways in the Drosophila brain.

title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Head and Neck Cancer: Integrated Evidence From TCGA Genomic Analysis and a US Multicenter Database Study.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Results remained consistent across sex, age, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, GLP-1RA type, and further sensitivity analyses. Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). GLP1R expression progressively decreased from normal to tumor and metastatic tissues, correlated with oncogenic mutation status, and was inversely associated with cell-cycle programs. title: Anti-obesity medications in people with kidney disease: a review.
abstract: Obesity accelerates progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), worsens cardiovascular risk and limits access to kidney transplantation. This narrative review summarises current evidence for anti-obesity medications in CKD. Traditional therapies provide modest weight loss and carry safety limitations, whereas incretin-based agents, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide, achieve substantial weight reduction with emerging renal benefits. Evidence remains limited in advanced CKD and dialysis populations.
summary_short: Obesity accelerates progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), worsens cardiovascular risk and limits access to kidney transplantation. This narrative review summarises current evidence for anti-obesity medications in CKD.

title: Mechanisms of kidney protection by semaglutide in type 2 diabetes and CKD.
Advances in GLP-2 research: mechanisms and therapeutic applications.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide 2 (GLP-2) is a proglucagon-derived peptide that is co-secreted with GLP-1 from intestinal endocrine L cells. The best-characterized actions of GLP-2 are its trophic and anti-inflammatory effects within the gastrointestinal tract. A GLP-2 analogue, teduglutide, has been utilized for the treatment of short bowel syndrome for over a decade, yet the actions and therapeutic potential of GLP-2 beyond the gut remain underexplored. GLP-2 exerts cardioprotective, hepatoprotective and immunomodulatory effects in preclinical studies, and circulating levels of GLP-2 correlate with the extent of tissue injury and sepsis in humans. GLP-2 also reduces gallbladder emptying and inhibits bone resorption. The actions of GLP-2 are transduced through a single GLP-2 receptor, which is expressed both within and external to the gut, including in the central nervous system, where its activation is associated with improved glucose homeostasis, attenuation of obesity-associated neuroinflammation and neuroprotection. In this Review, we highlight advances in our understanding of the effects of GLP-2 within and beyond the gut, highlighting the translational relevance of potential new indications and innovations in GLP-2 therapeutics, while discussing limitations and gaps in the existing data.
summary_short: The actions of GLP-2 are transduced through a single GLP-2 receptor, which is expressed both within and external to the gut, including in the central nervous system, where its activation is associated with improved glucose homeostasis, attenuation of obesity-associated neuroinflammation and neuroprotection.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and eye-related outcomes - A systematic review and meta-analysis. OphthoEvidence Report 1.
abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials examining the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) use across all clinical indications and ocular outcomes. GLP-1 RAs are widely used to manage diabetes, obesity, and other cardiometabolic conditions. However, their effects on diabetic retinopathy and other ocular outcomes remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to August 2025. Eligible trials compared any GLP-1 RAs with placebo, standard care or active comparator for patients with any clinical indication. Pairs of reviewers conducted study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessments independently. We performed random-effects meta-analyses and rated certainty of evidence using GRADE. A total of 142 trials enrolling 172,050 participants met eligibility criteria. Moderate to high certainty evidence suggests GLP-1 RAs probably increase the risk of diabetic retinopathy (odds ratio (OR) 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.15 [1.03-1.28]), vitreous hemorrhage (OR 95% CI 1.64 [1.08-2.49]), need for retinal procedures (OR 95% CI 1.37 [1.07-1.75]), total retinal vascular disorders (OR 95% CI 1.54 [1.12-2.12]), including retinal vascular occlusion (2.33 [1.22-4.45]). title: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. title: Brain insulin resistance in the development of obesity and type 2 diabetes: temporal trajectories in humans.
abstract: Brain insulin resistance might promote dysregulated eating and impaired systemic metabolism. This Review addresses the central question of temporality-whether brain insulin resistance precedes peripheral insulin resistance. We summarise human approaches to quantify brain insulin resistance and scalable biomarkers anchored to imaging-defined phenotypes. Across the metabolic continuum, alterations appear to emerge early in hypothalamic and mesolimbic systems and are modified by sex and metabolic health. Functional neuroimaging readouts often shift after modest lifestyle or pharmacological interventions, whereas insulin-stimulated brain glucose uptake might require more sustained systemic change. Evidence of hypothalamic gliosis suggests that inflammatory responses could link metabolic stress to impaired brain insulin action. Collectively, the data are consistent with a trajectory from diet-sensitive central alterations to later bidirectional reinforcement of central and peripheral insulin resistance, accelerating progression towards metabolic disease. GLP-1 receptor agonists, GLP-1/GIP dual agonists, and emerging multi-agonists may engage overlapping circuits, raising the possibility that part of their benefit arises from restoring, bypassing, or compensating for impaired brain insulin action.
summary_short: Evidence of hypothalamic gliosis suggests that inflammatory responses could link metabolic stress to impaired brain insulin action.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for alcohol use disorder: mechanisms, clinical evidence and testable predictions.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing condition characterized by disturbances in reward processing, stress responses, immune signaling, and metabolic regulation. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), originally developed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, have attracted attention as candidate treatments for AUD because they act on several of these interconnected pathways. This narrative review examines the neurobiological pathways shared by ethanol exposure and GLP-1 signaling, appraises preclinical and clinical evidence while distinguishing demonstrated effects from untested mechanisms, and derives testable predictions from a state-dependent translational model. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for literature published up to 15 July 2026 using terms related to GLP-1 receptor agonists, alcohol, reward circuitry, inflammation, metabolism, craving, and relapse; one randomized trial published after the search date was added during revision. Experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, observational investigations, and systematic reviews were synthesized narratively, and each finding was assigned a predefined evidence status (Established, Indirect, or Hypothesis). In rodent and non-human primate models, the GLP-1 receptor agonists exendin-4, liraglutide, exenatide, and semaglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide reduce alcohol consumption and relapse-like behavior and attenuate alco

title: Beyond the Classical Incretins: Is a Neural Enteroinsular Axis a Missing Link?
abstract: Article highlights The incretin effect (i.e., greater insulin release after oral versus intravenous glucose administration) is mainly due to the intestinal hormones glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP). However, growing evidence shows that GLP-1 and GIP do not fully explain the complexity of gut-to-islet communication. Gut-induced insulin secretion continues without GLP-1 and GIP receptors. However, denervating entero-pancreatic neurons abolishes the intestinal phase of preabsorptive insulin secretion, even if enteroendocrine cells and GLP-1 and GIP production are preserved. The entero-pancreatic neural circuit can directly modulate islet activity, suggesting the incretin effect may include the neural enteroinsular axis. Future studies should clarify how the neural enteroinsular axis regulates metabolic homeostasis.
summary_short: However, growing evidence shows that GLP-1 and GIP do not fully explain the complexity of gut-to-islet communication.

title: Quality of Care and Outcomes Among American Indian and Alaska Native Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: Cardiovascular Health Insights From the American Heart Association Get With The Guidelines Program.
abstract: Background American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients in the US face a disproportionate burden of cardiovascular disease, yet data on the quality of care and outcomes in this population are limited. Using the American Heart Association's Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease registry, we evaluated the clinical profiles and use of evidence-based therapies among AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction compared with White patients. Methods We analyzed data from 1955 AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction in 45 states participating in the Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease program from 2017 to 2022. Six performance measures were evaluated: aspirin within 24 hours, β-blocker and statin at discharge, smoking cessation counseling, ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor/ARB (angiotensin II receptor blocker) for EF ≤40%, and antiplatelet therapy at discharge. Additional metrics included door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes for ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction, cardiac rehabilitation referral, GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) use for those with obesity and diabetes, and in-hospital mortality. Results Compared with White patients, AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction were younger, with a higher prevalence of diabetes, obesity, and end-stage renal disease. title: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis.
abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. title: Autophagy activation partially alleviates endometrial dysfunction and cellular senescence induced by paracrine factors from BPA/BPAF-treated human endometrial stromal cells.
abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) and its substitute bisphenol AF (BPAF) are prevalent environmental endocrine disruptors found in industrial products. However, their effects on human endometrial stromal cells (hESCs) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain inadequately understood. This study investigates whether paracrine factors released by BPA/BPAF-induced senescent hESCs into conditioned medium can trigger senescence in neighboring healthy cells, and whether autophagy activation can attenuate this bystander damage. Conditioned media from senescent cells treated with BPA/BPAF were applied to young hESCs, resulting in a decrease in the expression of the decidualization marker PRL mRNA and a reduction in the area of trophoblast cell spread in BeWo co-cultures. Long-term exposure to BPA or BPAF compromises decidualization and the supportive functions of embryonic implantation. Additionally, increased SA-β-Gal staining positivity, G1-phase cell cycle arrest, and upregulation of p16, p21, and p53 at both mRNA and protein levels were observed. Rapamycin (Rapa) activated autophagy and thereby not only upregulated PRL mRNA expression and promoted trophoblast cell spreading, but also significantly reduced SA-β-Gal staining positivity, the G1-phase cell fraction, and p16, p21, and p53 expression at both transcriptional and translational levels. title: Dairy-derived bioactive peptides in the regulation of obesity and type 2 diabetes: engineered production strategies, mechanisms and translational challenges.
abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes are interrelated metabolic disorders and pose growing socioeconomic and clinical burdens. Although current pharmacotherapies, such as metformin and orlistat, are widely used, their long-term effectiveness may be constrained by side effects, poor compliance, and incomplete glycemic control in some patients. Hence, interest in food-derived peptides as sustainable dietary interventions for metabolic health has increased. Casein and whey proteins can generate peptides with potential anti-obesity and anti-diabetic activities by modulating digestive enzymes, incretin signaling, insulin sensitivity, and inflammation. However, evidence is predominantly from in vitro and animal studies, with limited human validation. Their clinical translation is further limited by bitterness, gastrointestinal instability, low bioavailability, and batch-to-batch variability. This review summarizes recent advances in peptide production, including fermentation, enzymatic hydrolysis, and synergistic production, and highlights mechanistic and translational challenges. The integration of AI and machine learning with advanced fermentation and enzymatic hydrolysis has, been reported to increase peptide yield and diversity. Engineering solutions, such as peptide self-assembly, nanoliposomes, nanofibers, and double-emulsion microencapsulation, may enhance peptide stability and delivery. title: Enhanced gemcitabine delivery <i>via</i> metformin-derived carbon dots for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma therapy.
abstract: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive cancer with a poor prognosis due to its dense stromal microenvironment, tumor heterogeneity, and rapid development of drug resistance. Gemcitabine (GEM), the FDA-approved first-line chemotherapy for PDAC, is often ineffective at standard doses, necessitating higher concentrations that lead to severe side effects. Metformin (MET), a widely used antidiabetic agent, has emerged as a potential stromal modulator that can reshape the PDAC tumor microenvironment. Here, we utilize non-toxic, fluorescent carbon dots (CDs) derived from MET (MetCDs) to enhance tumor targeting and reduce the effective dose of GEM in PDAC therapy, leveraging their favorable size, positive surface potential and structural resemblance to glutamine, a crucial amino acid for cancer cell proliferation. To enable comparative analysis, studies were parallelly conducted on carbon nitride dots, with negative surface potential, and selective cancer cell uptake. The successful conjugation of GEM to the CDs via carbodiimide coupling was confirmed through comprehensive optical, structural, and morphological analyses. A novel approach has been implemented to overcome the challenges associated with GEM quantification in highly photoactive drug carriers using circular dichroism spectroscopy. title: Treatment adherence and clinical response in adolescents with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
abstract: Objectives Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) commonly manifests during adolescence and requires sustained treatment. This study aimed to evaluate treatment initiation, adherence, and clinical response to different therapeutic modalities in adolescents with PMOS. Methods This observational study included 40 adolescents aged 14-18 years with PMOS who were evaluated and treated at a tertiary adolescent gynecology clinic. Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for baseline characteristics and recommended treatments, and a face-to-face questionnaire was used to assess treatment initiation, self-reported duration of uninterrupted adherence, and changes in clinical symptoms. Associations between treatment adherence, clinical response, and pediatric endocrinology consultation were evaluated. Results Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) were the most frequently recommended treatment (75.0 %, n=30). Treatment initiation rates were 83.3 % (n=25) for COCs, 36.8 % (n=7) for weight loss interventions, 100 % (n=5) for progesterone therapy, 66.7 % (n=2) for metformin, and 42.9 % (n=3) for laser hair removal. While 20 % of participants (n=8) reported never initiating the recommended treatments, only 10 % (n=4) maintained uninterrupted treatment adherence for longer than 6 months. Regression of menstrual irregularities was reported more frequently among participants with adherence for at least 3 months than among those with shorter adherence (82.6 % vs. 52.9 %, p=0.043); co

title: Developing and Externally Validating Machine Learning Models to Forecast Short-Term Risk of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.
abstract: Objectives To develop and externally validate supervised machine learning models using routinely collected ICU electronic health record (EHR) data to predict short-term onset of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) before clinical diagnosis. Design Prospective observational cohort study with temporal model development and external validation. Setting ICUs. Patients Mechanically ventilated adults in a prospective observational cohort (Successful Clinical Response In Pneumonia Therapy [SCRIPT]) who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) for suspected pneumonia and had BAL-confirmed adjudicated VAP or adjudicated non-VAP status (n = 507). External validation in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) included mechanically ventilated patients with greater than or equal to 48 hours of continuous invasive ventilation (n = 2681). Additional evaluation was performed in participants from the Inhaled Amikacin vs. Placebo to Prevent Ventilator Associated Pneumonia (AMIKINHAL) randomized trial evaluating inhaled amikacin for VAP prevention, using centrally adjudicated VAP outcomes. Interventions None. Measurements and main results We extracted 36 day-level clinical features (vital signs, ventilator settings, laboratory values, inflammatory markers, and support devices) from the EHR and trained models to predict VAP within 3, 5, or 7 days before BAL-confirmed diagnosis. Phenotyping of cardiac pathologies in Afro-caribbeans: a scoping review.
abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease (CVD) claims 18.6 million lives annually worldwide. Caribbean nations are particularly vulnerable to CVDs, as by Western standards they are largely comprised of racial/ethnic minorities and classified as Low-and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs); with race/ethnicity and socioeconomics affecting health outcomes. Cardiac pathology phenotypes (morphologic descriptions) can guide targeted diagnostics and therapeutics, yet despite this, there exists paucity of literature on Afro-Caribbean cardiac pathologies. This scoping review mapped existing cardiac pathology phenotyping literature across thirteen predominantly Black Caribbean nations and the diaspora; summarizing existing data, identifying gaps and setting the stage to prioritize future CVD cohort studies to reduce Afro-Caribbean under representation in the medical literature. Methods This review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Four academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Bireme - Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences), and Google Scholar were queried with predefined search terms to obtain articles in English between 1990 - 2025, with Afro-Caribbeans from 13 nations or diaspora (United States of America (USA), Europe or Canada), with cardiac pathology phenotyping data derived from ECG, imaging or autopsy. title: Rapidly Growing Fetal Cervical Mass: Prenatal Diagnostic Insights and Perinatal Management Considerations-A Case Report.
abstract: Fetal cervical masses are rare anomalies associated with significant perinatal morbidity due to potential airway obstruction. The main differential diagnoses are cervical teratoma and lymphatic malformation, two entities whose prognosis and management differ substantially. We report the case of a 38 year-old gravida 3 para 0 woman in whom a fetal anterior neck mass was identified at 17 weeks' gestation. Serial ultrasound demonstrated rapid growth with progressive solid-cystic components, calcifications, hypervascularity and polyhydramnios, whereas the fetal MRI report initially favored a cystic lymphatic malformation. Multidisciplinary evaluation favored a cervical teratoma; the EXIT strategy was ultimately ruled out primarily because predicted lethal pulmonary hypoplasia at a very early gestational age made survival unlikely even with a secured airway, and secondarily because massive tumor extension made airway access unlikely to succeed. Compassionate termination of pregnancy was offered; the parents opted for a planned cesarean delivery with neonatal comfort care, but spontaneous preterm labor occurred at 26 + 1 weeks and a stillborn male infant was delivered by emergency cesarean section. Postmortem examination confirmed a predominantly mature congenital cervical teratoma. This case illustrates the diagnostic value of serial imaging, the complementarity of ultrasound and MRI, and the centrality of multidisciplinary decision-making.
summary_short: Fetal cervical masses are rare anomalies associated with significant perinatal morbidity due to potential airway obstruction. We report the case of a 38 year-old gravida 3 para 0 woman in whom a fetal anterior neck mass was identified at 17 weeks' gestation.

title: Exosomes: Mechanisms of Action and Potential Therapeutic Applications for Diseases.
abstract: Exosomes are extracellular vesicles (EVs) of endosomal origin, whereas small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are defined by size without specifying biogenesis. These vesicles mediate intercellular communication through surface interactions and molecular cargo transfer, with effects that depend on their cellular source, composition, and recipient cells. This review summarizes current understanding of exosome biogenesis, cargo sorting, cellular uptake, and major modes of action. We then examine their roles across cancer, cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic, inflammatory, autoimmune, and infectious diseases, highlighting both shared mechanisms and disease-specific effects. We also discuss the development of EV-associated biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring, together with the use of natural and engineered vesicles as therapeutic agents and drug-delivery platforms. By linking immune regulation, cell-fate control, and metabolic remodeling across diseases, we examine how vesicle-mediated cellular responses influence disease progression and tissue repair, and discuss their implications for diagnosis and therapy. Clinical translation remains constrained by vesicle heterogeneity, methodological variability, manufacturing challenges, and limited evidence from controlled clinical studies. title: Nanomaterials for the treatment of aging-related diseases: applications, mechanisms and perspectives.
abstract: Aging-related diseases (ARDs) are a growing health burden caused by the progressive loss of physiological homeostasis. Aging is driven by interconnected molecular, cellular, and tissue alterations that create shared but heterogeneous pathological bases for these disorders. Conventional therapies often have limited access to pathological tissues and intracellular targets in ARDs. Nanomaterials offer distinct opportunities because their nanoscale dimensions and intrinsic physicochemical properties enable interactions with biological structures from subcellular compartments to aged tissue microenvironments. However, current evidence remains fragmented across nanomaterial design, aging mechanisms, disease contexts, and translational studies. This Review integrates nanomaterial design with aging biology to clarify how nanoscale physicochemical properties shape therapeutic behavior in ARDs. Particular emphasis is placed on the mechanisms by which nanomaterials modulate cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), restore proteostasis and autophagy, regulate mitochondrial homeostasis, alleviate oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, and promote tissue regeneration. These mechanisms are further related to major ARDs, including neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases, as well as cancer, highlighting how disease context and pathological mechanisms shape nanomaterial-based therapeutic strategies. summary_short: Aging-related diseases (ARDs) are a growing health burden caused by the progressive loss of physiological homeostasis. Aging is driven by interconnected molecular, cellular, and tissue alterations that create shared but heterogeneous pathological bases for these disorders.

title: Bayesian estimation of heritabilities and genetic correlations for ultrasound-measured carcass traits and body weight in Nelore cattle.
abstract: Weight and ultrasound-measured carcass traits were evaluated in 6,094 Nelore cattle, comprising 3,395 males and 2,699 females, with records collected between 2013 and 2024. The traits analyzed were body weight (BW), Longissimus muscle area (LMA), LMA adjusted per 100 kg of BW (LMA/100), muscle shape ratio (RATIO), marbling (MAR), subcutaneous fat thickness (SFT), and SFT adjusted per 100 kg of BW (SFT/100). Genetic parameters were estimated using a Bayesian multiple-trait animal model fitted by Gibbs sampling, in which all seven traits were analyzed simultaneously. Contemporary group and age at ultrasound measurement were included as fixed effects, whereas the animal additive genetic effect was fitted as random. Maternal effects were not included because each dam had only one offspring with a phenotypic record, precluding their reliable separation from direct additive genetic and residual effects. Posterior mean heritability estimates ranged from moderate to high, indicating exploitable additive genetic variation for growth, muscularity, marbling, and subcutaneous fat deposition. LMA/100 showed the highest heritability, although its interpretation should account for the statistical properties of ratio traits. Positive genetic correlations of BW with LMA and RATIO indicated that selection for increased body weight may produce favorable correlated responses in absolute muscularity and muscle conformation. title: An Integrated Tick Management (ITM) protocol combining strategic acaricide treatments and pasture management for cattle tick control.
abstract: The cattle tick Rhipicephalus microplus remains as a challenge for cattle production in tropical and subtropical regions. To date, R. microplus control has relied mainly on chemical acaricides. However, the widespread acaricide resistance has highlighted the need for alternative approaches for sustainable tick control. In this sense, Integrated Tick Management (ITM) is an approach that combines more than one strategy, aiming at long-term control with delayed resistance selection. Here, we evaluated, under field conditions, management practices that combine strategic acaricide treatments with pasture spelling. The approach was based on alternating cattle between infested and presumed tick-free (non-cattle-grazed) paddocks after defined strategic acaricide treatments, thereby allowing a pasture spelling period. Four groups of 20 animals were formed: two managed under ITM conditions, one using only chemical acaricides, and an untreated control group. At the beginning of the spring, the two groups selected for ITM received two successive acaricide treatments. After that, two groups were temporarily moved during summer to presumed tick-free paddocks for 49 days, allowing this time of pasture spelling. One of these paddocks had been previously used for rice cultivation, and the other one for sheep grazing. After this period, cattle returned to the original paddocks. title: Metabolomic Biomarkers in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) carries a mortality of approximately 40% and causes significant long-term disability. Delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI) affects approximately 30% of survivors and is a major determinant of poor outcome, yet no validated biomarker exists for its early prediction. Metabolomics-high-throughput profiling of small-molecule metabolites-offers a window into early metabolic disruptions that precede structural injury, but no systematic review has synthesised this evidence. MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 28 May 2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, including studies that applied metabolomic profiling (≥ 16 unique metabolites, or a validated untargeted nuclear magnetic resonance or mass spectrometry platform) to blood or cerebrospinal fluid in adult patients with aSAH and reported associations with DCI or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk-of-bias using the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool. Thirteen studies (733 patients; 2005-2026) were included. Four biological themes emerged-a systemic glycolytic shift with tricarboxylic acid cycle disruption; disruption of the arginine-nitric oxide axis, with plasma arginine depletion preceding DCI by 24-48 h (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.08-0.55%); alterations in taurine and excitatory amino acid metabolism, with plasma taurine predicti
summary_short: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) carries a mortality of approximately 40% and causes significant long-term disability. Delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI) affects approximately 30% of survivors and is a major determinant of poor outcome, yet no validated biomarker exists for its early prediction.

title: Scoping Review of Local Global Health Curricula in Undergraduate Medical Education and GREET Criteria Application.
abstract: Introduction Local global health education applies global health (GH) principles to local health challenges and helps medical students develop skills for working with vulnerable populations and in under-resourced settings. We present a scoping review to describe local GH curricula in undergraduate medical education and examine them using a validated education checklist (Guidelines for Reporting Evidence-based practice Educational interventions and Teaching (GREET)). Methods Nine databases were searched (2000-2024) for English-language articles describing local GH curricula or interventions for medical students. Other levels of healthcare trainees or interventions not pertinent to local GH principles were excluded. Results Of 6,445 abstracts, 42 full-text articles met inclusion criteria. Delivery formats included longitudinal programming, electives, lecture series, standardized patient simulations, and virtual exchanges. Underserved patient populations included Indigenous communities, immigrants/refugees/asylum seekers, rural populations, and low-income groups. Most studies ( n = 27) reported formal local and/or international partnership(s). GREET analysis showed strong reporting (> 85%) of core elements, including theory, instructors, planned delivery, and learning objectives. title: Temporal Trends of Mortality Due to Obesity in the United States, 1999-2022, an Analysis of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention WONDER Database: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Obesity, the excess body fat, is a chronic problem that disrupts both physical and mental health. Obesity is linked to diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, making it the second most frequent preventable cause leading to death. Contemporary national trends in obesity-related mortality, including the COVID-19 pandemic period, remain incompletely characterized. We therefore examined temporal trends in obesity-related mortality in the United States from 1999 to 2022 by sex, age group, census region, and place of death. Methods Deidentified data from CDC WONDER database were used in our study. The International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) code E66 was used to identify cases in which obesity was recorded as an underlying or contributing cause of death between 1999 and 2022. The data were extracted based on age, gender, year, population size, census region, and place of death. Annual percent changes (APC) and age adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100,000 people were utilized in our study to analyse the mortality trends of Obesity in the United States using Joinpoint regression. Results During 1999-2022, obesity caused 840,975 deaths in the United States. The Obesity AAMR was 4.7 per 100,000 in 1999, which rose to 18.9 in 2022, after a peak of 24.73 in 2021. title: Efficacy and safety of incretin-based therapies on depressive symptoms in individuals with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus: A frequentist and Bayesian meta-analysis.
abstract: Incretin-based therapies are increasingly prescribed for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, conditions frequently comorbid with depression. Preclinical evidence suggests GLP-1 receptor activation modulates neurotransmitter systems and neuroinflammatory pathways implicated in the pathophysiology of depression. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the efficacy and safety of incretin-based therapies on depressive symptom scores using both frequentist and Bayesian frameworks. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, CENTRAL, and ICTRP was conducted, and randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1 receptor agonists or DPP-4 inhibitors in adults regardless of T2DM that reported validated depression scale scores were included. The primary outcome was change in depressive symptom scores, summarised as standardized mean differences (SMD). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Frequentist meta-analysis done on eleven RCTs (n = 5516) demonstrated a small but statistically significant reduction in depressive symptom scores with incretin-based therapies (SMD= -0.08; 95%CI: -0.14 to -0.02; I²=0%). Bayesian analysis corroborated this finding (SMD = -0.09; 95%CrI: -0.19 to -0.01; τ=0.09). Liraglutide demonstrated the most consistent subgroup signal. title: A Phase 2, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Acmopatide (CT-868), a Fully Biased GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acmopatide, a signal-biased glucagon-like peptide 1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight or obesity. Research design and methods In this phase 2, 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study, adults with T1D (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%; BMI ≥27 kg/m2) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to once-daily subcutaneous acmopatide (1.8, 4.1, or 6.6 mg) or volume-matched placebo. The primary end point was change from baseline (CFB) in HbA1c (%) at week 16; secondary end points included percent CFB in body weight and insulin dose. Results Overall, 111 participants were randomized (placebo n = 29, acmopatide 1.8 mg n = 27, 4.1 mg n = 28, 6.6 mg n = 27). Mean (SD) baseline HbA1c was 7.5% (0.6), and mean BMI was 34.3 (5.6) kg/m2. Acmopatide improved HbA1c (least squares [LS] mean CFB -0.4 to -0.6% vs. -0.3% with placebo; nominally significant placebo-adjusted difference for 4.1 mg: -0.3% [90% CI -0.6 to -0.1]; P = 0.020). title: An Incretin-Dependent Modulation of Periprandial Neutrophilia.
abstract: Daily cycles of fasting and feeding shape systemic metabolism, yet how innate immunity senses these transitions remains unclear. Chronic high-fat diet (HFD) primes granulocyte-monocyte progenitors to generate clones with heightened inflammasome activity and excessive production of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and IL-1β. Whether periprandial states influence immune surveillance remains unknown. We profiled periprandial immune adaptations in mice fed an HFD (60% energy from fat) or standard-fat diet (SFD) after overnight fasting and up to 4 h postfeeding, integrating blood immunophenotyping, endotoxin challenges, and neutrophil activation markers. Neutrophil counts rose within 15 min of feeding, preceding monocytosis (≥2-4 h). Neutrophilia during SFD, but not HFD, refeeding was associated with lower lipopolysaccharide-induced sickness, suggesting that it is critical for the host to microbial challenges. This early neutrophilia was enhanced by HFD and further amplified with the establishment of insulin resistance following 7 days of HFD feeding. We link this response to intestinal fat absorption and to the coordinated glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)/insulin regulation of the periprandial responses. Yet, GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) antagonism potentiated neutrophilia during HFD feeding, whereas coadministration of insulin abolished it. summary_short: Neutrophilia during SFD, but not HFD, refeeding was associated with lower lipopolysaccharide-induced sickness, suggesting that it is critical for the host to microbial challenges.

title: Olive Oil Before Oral Glucose Delays Gastric Emptying and Lowers Glycemia Through Partially Redundant Glucagon and GLP-1 Signaling in Mice.
abstract: Consumption of fat before carbohydrate (preload) attenuates postprandial glucose excursions, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether an olive oil preload (OG) reduces glycemia by engaging endocrine and neural regulation of gastric emptying. Wild-type C57BL/6J mice received OG or olive oil after (GO) an oral glucose load, with a water preload (WG) as control. Glucose, insulin, glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and gastric emptying were assessed. Studies were also performed in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, NSY diabetic mice, Gcg-deficient and Glp1r-deficient mice, mice receiving glucagon and/or GLP-1 receptor blockade, and mice subjected to bilateral subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve ligation (VNL). Compared with WG and GO, OG reduced the early glucose excursion and slowed gastric emptying, accompanied by increased glucagon, GIP, and GLP-1 secretion. Similar effects were evident in diabetic mice. The response was absent in Gcg-deficient mice but largely preserved in Glp1r-deficient mice and following blockade of either receptor alone. Combined receptor blockade attenuated glucose lowering and eliminated detectable gastric slowing, supporting partially redundant signaling. VNL attenuated these effects, despite preserved or enhanced hormone secretion, supporting a contribution of vagal signaling. title: Management of Type 2 Diabetes, 2026. A Consensus Report by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD).
abstract: The American Diabetes Association and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes convened a panel to update the consensus statement on the management of type 2 diabetes in nonpregnant adults, published since 2006 and last updated in 2022. The target audience is the multidisciplinary health care team providing diabetes care in the U.S. and Europe. A systematic examination of publications since 2022 informed new recommendations. This update has broadened the focus from the management of hyperglycemia to the holistic management of type 2 diabetes and its risk of associated multiple long-term conditions. Fundamental aspects of diabetes care include promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors (healthy eating, 24-h physical behaviors including sleep, and avoiding tobacco and substance use), alongside the provision of psychological support and weight management interventions. For the management of people living with type 2 diabetes, earlier use, potentially from diagnosis, of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)-based therapies to offer organ protection and improve long-term outcomes in type 2 diabetes is advocated. Furthermore, earlier combination use of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1-based therapies should be considered in people with concomitant cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure. title: Nonmedical Factors That Influence Diabetes Complications and Multilevel Strategies to Reduce Disparities and Improve Outcomes in the U.S.
abstract: The development of diabetes complications is complex and multifactorial. Although advances in pharmacologic interventions and technology have improved diabetes management, nonmedical factors continue to drive persistent disparities in complications across the U.S. Using a socioecological framework, we examine how nonmedical factors operating at individual, organizational, community, and policy levels contribute to rising complications rates. We synthesize multilevel evidence-based interventions, real-world examples, and emerging opportunities that address these drivers. Approaches include culturally and linguistically tailored, digitally delivered diabetes education; systematic screening and documentation of social drivers within health care systems; use of health information systems technology; training for health care providers; multisector community partnerships that leverage social care resources; and policy incentives that integrate medical and social care. Coordinated interventions across socioecological levels are essential to move beyond traditional clinical approaches toward equitable, sustainable diabetes care that reduces complications.
summary_short: Although advances in pharmacologic interventions and technology have improved diabetes management, nonmedical factors continue to drive persistent disparities in complications across the U.S.

title: Evaluating the Strength of Instrumental Variables in in the Evaluation of Time-Varying Treatments.
abstract: There is a growing interest in the use of instrumental variable analysis to evaluate time-varying treatments in comparative effectiveness research. In this setting, a major challenge is to identify an instrumental variable that is strongly associated with treatment assignment at each time point. The strength of association of an instrument is often assessed using the F-statistic. However, the standard F-statistic assumes that the instrument and the treatment are homoscedastic and serially uncorrelated, which is unrealistic in the evaluation of time-varying treatments. This paper proposes the use of a robust F-statistic that allows for the autocorrelated and heteroskedastic nature of time-varying instruments. A simulation study assesses the relative performance of the proposed F-statistic in comparison to standard, commonly used F-statistics. We illustrate the practical advantages of the different approaches in an evaluation of second-line oral anti-diabetic treatments among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus in the UK.
summary_short: In this setting, a major challenge is to identify an instrumental variable that is strongly associated with treatment assignment at each time point.

title: The Joint Effects of Life's Essential 8 and Genetics on Mild Cognitive Impairment and Dementia Risk in People With Diabetes: Findings From the UK Biobank and All of Us.
abstract: Objective We examined how cardiovascular health (CVH), measured by Life's Essential 8 (LE8), and genetic risk are jointly associated with risks of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and related cognitive outcomes in people with diabetes. Research design and methods We analyzed 41,374 participants without dementia from the UK Biobank (UKB) and 9,766 from All of Us (AoU). LE8, comprising diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep, BMI, lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure, was scored from 0 to 100 and categorized as low, moderate, or high. Genetic risk was assessed using APOE ε4 alleles and polygenic risk scores (PRS) for Alzheimer disease. We used Cox regression to examine associations of LE8 with MCI and dementia and linear regression to assess MRI-based brain functional measures and cognitive test outcomes, adjusting for covariates. Interactions between LE8 and genetic risk were tested on multiplicative and additive scales. Results Over 15 years of follow-up (UKB), moderate or high CVH versus low CVH was associated with a lower risk of MCI (hazard ratio 0.82 [95% CI 0.71, 0.95], P Conclusions Better CVH was significantly associated with a lower risk of MCI in people with diabetes, accounting for genetic risk. The association between CVH and MCI and dementia was stronger among individuals with low or moderate genetic risk and appeared attenuated among those with high genetic risk.

title: Changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year after kidney transplantation
abstract: Pre-transplant senescence biomarkers are associated with frailty in patients undergoing kidney transplantation (KT). We examined the relationship between changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year post-KT. Plasma concentrations of senescence biomarkers, frailty (Physical Frailty Phenotype), and physical function (Short Physical Performance Battery) were simultaneously measured. Relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator methods were used to select variables for multivariable models. Among 188 participants, mean age was 53 ± 13 years, 62% were male, 34% had diabetes, and 30% underwent deceased donor KT. During the first year after KT, age ≥ 60 was associated with smaller reductions in GDF-15 and IL-8, whereas Black race was associated with greater reduction in RAGE. Alemtuzumab was associated with smaller reduction in IL-7 compared to other induction agents, whereas deceased donor KT was associated with greater reduction in PAI-1. On multivariable analysis, more improvement in frailty was significantly associated with reduction in uPAR concentrations (β − 0.23, 95% CI − 0.38 to − 0.08, p = 0.003). Changes in biomarker concentrations were not independently associated with changes in physical function. Whether interventions affecting the abundance or behavior of senescent cells may counter frailty in KT recipients warrants further exploration. Graphical Abstract

title: Influence of regional white matter lesion volume differences related to cardiorespiratory fitness on cognition in healthy older adults
abstract: Greater cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) has been associated with reduced global burden of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions, a neuroimaging marker of small vessel cerebrovascular disease, and lower risk of age-related cognitive impairment and dementia. However, little is known about how CRF relates to regional patterns of WMH volume and the associated impact on cognitive aging. In a cohort of 166 community-dwelling, healthy older adults (mean age = 70.49 ± 9.96 years, 48.8% women), we investigated the association of CRF with regionally distributed WMH burden using multivariate regional network analysis of hemispheric lobar WMH volumes. We additionally evaluated the moderating role of CRF-related regional WMH volumetric differences for cognition. Higher CRF, distinct from self-reported habitual physical activity, was associated with a distributed covariance pattern of WMH volume reductions in bilateral frontal and right parietal lobes, with relative increases in bilateral occipital lobes. Greater CRF-WMH pattern expression was associated with younger age and male sex. Additionally, there was a significant age-by-CRF-WMH network pattern interaction for memory, but not for information processing speed and executive functioning, such that the higher the pattern expression, the weaker the inverse association between age and memory performance. title: Aging impairs CX3CL1 neuroprotection in α-synuclein-induced Parkinson’s disease pathology
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD), the second most prevalent movement disorder, is pathologically defined by the accumulation of α-synuclein (α-syn), loss of dopaminergic neuron and inflammation in the substantia nigra pars compacta. The neuronally expressed chemokine CX3CL1 (fractalkine, FKN), when delivered as the soluble form (sFKN) via AAV-mediated overexpression, protects dopamine neurons in several animal models of PD. Since aging is a major risk factor for PD, we examined the effects of sFKN overexpression in both young and aged PD models. To model PD, young (3-month) and aged (15-month) male F344 rats received unilateral intracranial injections of recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (rAAV9) encoding either human wild-type α-synuclein (α-syn) or green fluorescent protein (GFP). Motor performance was evaluated at baseline, 1 month, and 2 months post-injection. Behavioral deficits and neuropathological changes were compared across treatment and age groups. CX3CL1 involvement in PD-related neuroinflammation was assessed using immunohistochemistry and biochemical analyses and bulk RNA-seq was used to characterize transcriptomic changes. We found that sFKN rescued both motor deficits and dopaminergic neuron loss in young PD animals but not in aged animals. Analysis of the transcriptomics revealed age-dependent alterations in inflammatory, immune, and neurogenic signaling in response to sFKN treatment. We found that sFKN rescued both motor deficits and dopaminergic neuron loss in young PD animals but not in aged animals.

title: Molecular PET imaging of cellular senescence: from current tracers to emerging biomarker-driven strategies
abstract: Cellular senescence is a dynamic and multifaceted biological process that contributes to aging and a wide spectrum of age-related diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders. Despite increasing recognition of its pathological significance, the ability to quantify senescence noninvasively in vivo remains a major limitation, particularly for longitudinal studies and therapeutic evaluation. Positron emission tomography (PET) offers a powerful platform to address this gap by enabling quantitative imaging of molecular processes in living systems. Recent advances have led to the development of PET radiotracers targeting senescence-associated features, including lysosomal β-galactosidase activity, cell-surface markers (uPAR), and intracellular accumulation products (lipofuscin). These first-generation approaches have established proof-of-concept for imaging senescence biology; however, they primarily reflect downstream hallmarks and have been largely evaluated in non-central nervous system (CNS) models, while their ability to quantify senescent-cell burden in naturally aged tissues and the CNS remains insufficiently established. Emerging evidence motivates the study of biomarker-driven and pathway-oriented imaging strategies that may provide complementary information about senescence-associated molecular mechanisms without necessarily offering greater biological specificity. title: Neuroprotective effects of metformin on cognition, mTOR, and inflammatory cytokines in a scopolamine-induced cognitive impairment model in ovariectomized rats.
abstract: Metformin, with its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, exhibits protective activity on the central nervous system (CNS). This study examined metformin's impact on anxiety-related cognitive deficits and hippocampal level of cytokines in Alzheimer's (AD)-like and ovariectomized rats. Eighty female Wistar rats were divided into eight groups: control, sham, ovariectomy (ovx), scopolamine (sco), ovariectomy +scopolamine (ovx + sco), metformin + scopolamine (met + sco), metformin + ovariectomy (met + ovx), and metformin + ovariectomy + scopolamine (met + ovx+sco). Morris Water Maze (MWM), Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) tests, Nissl and Thioflavin staining, ELISA, and Western Blot were used. In all groups, Metformin was administered before intraperitoneal injection of scopolamine and before ovariectomy surgery.MWM behavioral test results showed that metformin improved spatial memory in impaired groups (SCO, OVX + SCO and OVX). The EPM behavioral test indicated that metformin could improve the increased anxiety levels found in the impaired groups. Nissl staining revealed the neuronal damage in the rats of the impaired group. Thioflavin staining showed that metformin reduced the number of beta-amyloid plaques in the treatment groups. title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Lipedema: A Clinical Observational Study.
abstract: Objective Lipedema is a painful, progressive disorder of adipose tissue that predominantly affects women. Conservative treatment often provides limited symptom relief, frequently necessitating surgical intervention. Emerging hypotheses suggest metabolic alterations within lipedema adipose tissue. Against this background, this study evaluated clinical and patient-reported outcomes in patients with lipedema treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted in patients with lipedema treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists. Patients subsequently underwent structured interviews assessing patient-reported changes in regional circumference and lipedema-related symptoms. Body weight and height were objectively measured, and BMI was calculated accordingly. Outcomes were analyzed using distribution-appropriate statistical tests. title: D-Xylose Attenuates High-Fat Diet-Induced Obesity Potentially via Modulation of Gut Microbiota and Cecal Lipidome in Mice.
abstract: Obesity and its associated metabolic complications pose a significant global public health challenge. This study systematically investigated the effects of D-xylose on gut microbiota structure and cecal lipid metabolism in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mouse model. Following a 12-week intervention, D-xylose supplementation inhibited HFD-induced weight gain, improved lipid profiles, and reduced serum levels of the endotoxin lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-6, as well as alleviating hepatic steatosis. Furthermore, it ameliorated intestinal villus damage and colonic mucus layer thickening. D-xylose enriched beneficial bacterial genera (e.g., Muribaculum, Akkermansia ) while suppressing obesity-linked taxa. In addition, D-xylose reversed excessive triglyceride and free fatty acid accumulation in the cecum induced by HFD and regulated bioactive lipid classes, including sphingolipids and phospholipids. Co-occurrence network analysis indicated that D-xylose intervention stabilized the interactions between gut microbiota and lipid metabolites. In conclusion, our findings suggest that D-xylose may alleviate metabolic disorders through associations with alterations in gut microbiota, enhancing intestinal barrier function, reducing systemic inflammation, and improving lipid homeostasis. This provides crucial preclinical evidence for developing D-xylose as a functional dietary component against obesity and related metabolic syndromes.

Tirzepatide in Maintenance Dialysis Patients With Obesity Previously Treated With Semaglutide: A Prospective Exploratory Observational Study of Weight and Body Composition.
abstract: Background/aims Obesity is a common modifiable barrier to kidney transplantation in patients on dialysis. We assessed whether switching to the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide reduces body weight and fat mass in individuals on dialysis previously treated with semaglutide. Materials and methods In this prospective exploratory observational study, adults on maintenance dialysis with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ) were switched from semaglutide to tirzepatide after failure to reach the transplant listing threshold or reported intolerance. The primary endpoint was the relative change in body weight from baseline to Week 12. Secondary endpoints were the changes in BMI, fat mass assessed by bioimpedance spectroscopy, and abdominal obesity assessed by waist-to-hip ratio, together with tolerability. Results We report on 17 patients (mean age 58.5 ± 9.0 years; 13 [76%] male; 7 haemodialysis, 10 peritoneal dialysis; mean BMI 35.8 ± 2.7 kg/m 2 ). title: Complementary Metabolic Effects of Exercise and GLP-1-Based Pharmacotherapy in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Multilevel Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Aims To assess exercise added to glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based pharmacotherapy and pharmacotherapy added to care incorporating exercise or physical-activity advice in Type 2 diabetes. Materials and methods Five databases were searched through 6 October 2026. Two- and three-level random-effects models included selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/GLP-1 receptor agonist. Bias and certainty were assessed. Adherence and harms were summarised. Results Of 16 732 records, 24 reports represented 23 independent studies. title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis.
abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability. 1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly, 2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure. 4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles. 5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. title: Dorsal Raphe Serotonergic Neurons at the Metabolic-Cognitive Interface: Converging Mechanisms, Causal Gaps, and Testable Predictions for Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment.
abstract: Background Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is clinically heterogeneous, yet the neural mechanism linking metabolic disturbance to selective cognitive-circuit dysfunction remains unresolved. We evaluated whether dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons could form a metabolic-cognitive interface. Methods PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase and Scopus were searched from inception to 2 August 2026. We synthesised 62 full-text-verified original studies, assessing serotonergic identity, raphe source, projection specificity, transmitter/receptor mediation, causal directness and translational relevance. Results DRN serotonergic populations are molecularly, physiologically and projectionally heterogeneous and integrate metabolic signals through afferents, GABAergic/glutamatergic circuitry and 5-HT1A feedback. Insulin has the strongest cell-defined support; evidence for leptin, GLP-1, ghrelin and orexin differs in causal resolution. Diabetes-associated changes in tissue 5-HT, SERT, receptor availability, evoked release and DRN excitability vary by region, stage, sex and model. DRN serotonergic pathways modulate hippocampal and prefrontal computations in non-diabetic models, but a complete diabetes-specific pathway from defined DRN remodelling to projection-selective dysfunction and cognition remains unproven. We evaluated whether dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons could form a metabolic-cognitive interface.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Risk of Liver Disease Progression and Decompensation in Metabolic Liver Disease.
abstract: Introduction Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) are major contributors to cirrhosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated benefits in obesity and type 2 diabetes and may reduce liver disease progression. This study evaluated the association between GLP-1 RA use and liver disease progression in patients with metabolic liver disease. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with obesity or type 2 diabetes and a diagnosis of MASLD or MASH treated at a single academic center from 2017 to 2024. Patients were stratified by GLP-1 RA exposure. Outcomes included progression to cirrhosis and hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis. Multivariable analyses adjusted for age, sex, race, rurality, and comorbidity burden. Results A total of 2,851 patients were included, of whom 852 received GLP-1 RAs and 1,999 did not. GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower rates of progression to cirrhosis and hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis. Progression to cirrhosis occurred in 216 GLP-1 RA users (25.4%, 95% CI: [22.5%, 28.4%]) and 588 non-users (29.4%, 95% CI: [27.5%, 31.5%]). Hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis occurred in 44 GLP-1 RA users (5.2%, 95% CI: [3.9%, 6.9%]) and 218 non-users (10.9%, 95% CI: [9.6%, 12.3%]). title: Effect of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy on Spinal Fusion Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Spinal fusion remains the benchmark procedure for degenerative spine disease, but outcomes are frequently limited by complications such as pseudarthrosis and revision surgery. With the rise in glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use for diabetes and weight management, interest has grown in their effects on bone metabolism and fusion healing. This study evaluated the association between GLP-1 RA therapy and outcomes after spinal fusion, including pseudarthrosis, revision surgery, perioperative complications, and length of stay. Methods A systematic review of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library was conducted to identify adults undergoing cervical or lumbar fusion through September 2025. Data on study design, GLP-1 exposure, spinal region, and outcomes were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted for pseudarthrosis outcomes. Results Twelve retrospective cohort studies and two reviews were included. All cohort studies carried at least moderate risk of bias, with three judged at serious risk; none achieved a low ROBINS-I rating. GRADE certainty was low for pseudarthrosis and length of stay and very low for revision surgery, infection, and other complications. title: Self-Active Lipid Nanocapsules Induce GLP‑1 Receptor-Dependent Signaling and Enhance Glucose-Stimulated Insulin Secretion.
abstract: Nanocarriers are typically designed as inert delivery platforms whose biological activity depends on their payloads. Here, we show that blank lipid nanocapsules (LNCs), in the absence of any loaded drug, are intrinsically bioactive and induce glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R)-dependent signaling in pancreatic β-cells. In MIN6 cells and isolated mouse islets, LNCs increased intracellular cAMP (∼2.5- and ∼2.7-fold, respectively) and potentiated glucose-stimulated insulin secretion up to twofold under high glucose, without altering basal secretion. These effects were prevented by the GLP-1R antagonist Exendin-9, the PKA inhibitor H89, and GLP-1R silencing, indicating dependence on GLP-1R receptor signaling. In vivo, intraperitoneal administration of blank LNCs, a route that avoids direct luminal exposure of the intestine and GLP-1 secretion, improved glucose tolerance in healthy and diabetic mice via a GLP-1R-dependent mechanism. The effects of blank LNCs are mimicked by medium-chain fatty acids (caprylic and capric acids), which recapitulated GLP-1R activation and insulinotropic responses. Lipase inhibition abolished both LNCs-induced signaling and functional effects, demonstrating the requirement for triglyceride core processing. Thus, blank LNCs activate GLP-1R signaling in β-cells through an indirect, lipid-mediated mechanism, revealing a previously unrecognized, payload-independent bioactivity of lipid nanocarriers beyond cargo delivery.

title: Primary Mediastinal Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma Involving the Superior Vena Cava in an Adult: An Extremely Rare Entity.
abstract: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) is a rare vascular tumour predominantly affecting infants. Primary mediastinal involvement in adults is exceptionally rare. We report a rare adult case mimicking thymoma but involving the superior vena cava (SVC). A 29-year-old male presented with an anterior mediastinal mass suspected as thymoma. Imaging revealed a solid lesion and the patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy. Intraoperatively, the tumour showed dense adherence to the SVC, necessitating SVC plasty. Histopathology confirmed KHE. The patient recovered uneventfully. Although KHE is primarily a paediatric diagnosis, it must be considered in the differential diagnosis of adult anterior mediastinal masses. Complete surgical resection remains the treatment of choice, though vascular reconstruction may be required due to the tumour's infiltrative nature.
summary_short: We report a rare adult case mimicking thymoma but involving the superior vena cava (SVC).

title: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon revealed by a rehabilitation referral for upper-limb heaviness in an adult with a giant hepatic haemangioma: a case report.
abstract: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon (KMP) is a consumptive coagulopathy arising within a vascular tumour. It is exceptional in adults, where a giant hepatic haemangioma is the usual substrate. We report a 42-year-old woman referred for physical and rehabilitation medicine assessment of a 3-day heaviness of the left upper limb; brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained for a suspected stroke was normal. The disability contrasted with a normal neurological examination, while complete physical examination found tenderness over the liver. A blood count showed haemoglobin at 7 g/dl with reticulocytosis and platelets falling from 25 to 6 × 10 9 /l. Ultrasound, computed tomography, and MRI showed a 112 × 100 mm centrally liquefied hepatic mass with progressive centripetal enhancement, indicating a bleeding giant haemangioma with KMP. Emergency transarterial embolization was decided, but the patient died in the angiography suite from fulminant haemorrhagic shock. A functional limb complaint may be the only visible sign of a lethal consumptive coagulopathy.
